rows.source: storm L1-21 (survived) + L2-02 (killed, format part) + scale.md format rows + robustness-v2 + research (Socialinsider, Buffer, Metricool) + a16z §1 + karoslabs/kindlyyours/sitti/xodigital/geektime syntheses
rows.lesson: No format wins everywhere. Pick the format from the client's own audience and the job the post has to do, not from habit or a platform-wide ranking. A carousel is the starting point only for accounts built on text and pictures, and it is judged on saves, sends and completion, not reach.
rows.scope: all clients: the mechanism is L1, the format weights are per client (DNA) with a kit fallback
rows.mechanism: 04h-select-format reads per-client format multipliers from the weekly own-grid read (shrunk toward the kit prior). When the client has no measured data it uses the kit's format mix. Every run logs the format, so the loop measures it.
rows.value: Kit/DNA param `format` weights, e.g. geektime {image .5, carousel-2 .35, reel .15}; hankypanky {carousel .7, reel .3}; sitti {reel for reach, carousel for series}.
rows.evidence: Within accounts (183 accounts, one vote each), format has no L1 signal: carousel +0.04 (76+/62-, p=0.27), reel -0.03 (59+/74-, p=0.23), image 0.00 (44+/43-, p=1.0). In robustness-v2, grouping accounts by format_mix has no predictive skill in any cut (perm_p 0.25-0.67). The industry signs reverse. Hebrew news: reel -0.27 (2+/8-, p=0.11), but that is sponsorship and freshness, not format. Music: reel -0.25 (0+/3-). Luxury: image -0.27 (1+/7-, p=0.07) and reel +0.19 (8+/3-). Intimates are neutral (percentile 0.49/0.51/0.49). Karos peers: carousels 1.41-1.80x on carousel-led audiences and 0.37-0.56x on reel-trained ones (@nogood.io, @orenmeetsworld). Platform research agrees on direction only: carousels lead engagement and saves (Socialinsider 0.50% vs 0.48% vs 0.33%; Metricool about 9x the saves of images), Reels lead reach (+36%), and single-image reach fell 22% year on year. a16z: carousels 1.14x, images 0.80x, reels 0.90x (one account). DT's April finding 'reels 10x, adopt reels' was a cross-account artefact of one account's style. Every industry cut is under 25 accounts, so none reaches L2.

extent.note: The account is too small to measure (22 followers). Keep carousels for the house series and run reels only as TRY slots until the peer test shows the audience is carousel-led.
Single image by default (75% of the house feed). A carousel only as a 2-slide hook-then-receipt. Reels only with native footage (Doom 13.36x), never sponsored clips.
Carousels in a16z's families (archival and manifesto). Judge reels on views only, because likes are hidden. Talking-head promo reels are demoted (a16z 0.19x median).
Carousel-first: its own carousels run 1.15x against 0.71x for reels (n=16/17).
Short reels (15 s or less) carry reach. Carousels of 4-7 wordless slides carry product and fit.
Founder and discovery reels for reach while the account is under 1K followers (8,620 views, 14x followers). Carousels for the repeatable series only.
Capybara reels are the only reach (9,902 views on 385 followers). Carousels only for proof and rule explainers.
The page's own best posts are short, bright party reels (median 16 s). Market carousels come as 2-slide cards or all-video decks. Plain single images only for news (0.21 otherwise).
Photo carousels plus reels. Single images rare: luxury image is 1+/7-, so this is a TRY weight pending its own grid.

rows.source: research (Instagram recommendation guidelines; Mosseri 30 Apr 2026 originality extension; Mosseri Oct 2024 on music in carousels) + storm L1-21 (survived) + don-techno footage gates
rows.lesson: Anything that could reach Reels or recommendation surfaces must be eligible for them: no other platform's watermark, full 1080-wide resolution, no letterbox borders, not previously posted, and only licensed or original music on business accounts.
rows.scope: all clients, all reels, and carousels carrying video slides or music
rows.mechanism: A pre-package gate on every video or audio asset: watermark and sticker detector, resolution ≥1080 wide on the chosen rendition, border detector, perceptual-hash check against the client's own grid, and an audio source that is licensed or the original upload.
rows.value: Per client: whether music is allowed (brand kit) and which licensed library to use.
rows.evidence: Instagram's recommendation guidelines deprioritise Reels that are watermarked, low-resolution, bordered or previously posted. On 30 Apr 2026 Mosseri extended the originality rule to photos and carousels at account level (majority of posts over a rolling 30 days). Mosseri: adding music makes a carousel eligible for Reels-tab surfaces. DT: 41% of 610 sampled TikToks carried a text sticker, and stickers killed 64 of 129 popping clips. This is primary platform policy, not a performance estimate.

extent.note: Publisher: own, partner or licensed footage only. The aggregator norm of 'credit plus repost' does not apply.

Regulated category: expect little recommendation reach whatever the eligibility. Lean on sends and search.

rows.source: storm L1-18 (survived; slide-count prescriptions refuted) + L1-13 (survived) + scale.md slides rows + research (Meta Feed card, Mosseri, Eden) + a16z §2.7 + karoslabs/sitti/hankypanky/kindlyyours/xodigital syntheses + owner letter I
rows.lesson: Slide count is not a lever in itself. The deck is as long as the number of distinct facts or pictures it has. Never pad and never recap. Slide 2 works as a second cover. The kit or DNA sets a band, but no global cap applies below the platform maximum.
rows.scope: all carousels: the rule is L1, the band is a kit/DNA value
rows.mechanism: Planner: slide count = the count of distinct facts or pictures, clipped to the band. WS-09 set-integrity gate: no duplicate or same-point slides and no recap slide (owner letter I). Slide 2 is gated with the cover's size and word rules.
rows.value: Band per kit/DNA: karoslabs 5-7; sitti 6-8 (cover, 4-6 spots, closer); hankypanky 3-6; kindlyyours 4-7; xodigital 5-7; geektime 1-2 (more only if each adds a fact); pitch 2 / 5-10 photo sequence / 6-10 manifesto; dontechno 2 or 6-10 video; n3 6-10 photo sequence (TRY).
rows.evidence: Within accounts: slides median(best-worst) is 0 over 169 accounts. 63+/37- (sign p=0.012) leans longer, but that is confounded with carousel vs single/reel (carousel alone +0.04, ns), so it argues only against capping short. Industry: luxury +1 (8+/5-, p=0.58); music -1 (2+/5-, p=0.45). Pooled evidence conflicts: Karos peers 5-7 1.43x vs 2-4 1.00x vs 11+ 0.98x (163 carousels, pooled across accounts); a16z 4-6 1.75x vs 9-12 0.66x (one account, long ones are explainers); DT market U-shape (2: 1.17, 3: 0.91, 4-5: 0.97, 6-7: 1.23, 8-10: 1.44, 11+: 1.49); Eden 3 slides 23.4% vs 14-20 slides ~32% at 2x (correlational, likes not completion). Meta's June 2026 Feed card scores completion with card count as an input. Mosseri: unengaged carousels are re-served from slide 2. Defects seen in our runs: Sitti slides 7-8 identical, Kindly byte-identical renders, XO one idea across 5 of 8 slides. No per-industry count survives a sign test, so the bands are authored defaults, not measured levers.

2 (claim plus proof) or 6-10 footage slides from one night. Avoid 3-5.

rows.source: owner letters L/N + owner promotion ladder (2026-09-22: 3 winners → client rule, replicates in 2-3 clients → industry, 1-in-10 experiments) + don-techno formats.yaml new_format_contract + a16z §5.1.9

rows.scope: all clients, all series and formats

DT formats.yaml runs 15 formats under this contract. a16z's explainer series fell from about 1.0x to 0.46x over 5 editions, so series decay and need a retire rule. The engine picks series deterministically (editorial-series.ts) and promotes templates on review (09f), but no series has market evidence and nothing retires one on results.

rows.source: storm L1-14 (killed) + karoslabs/sitti/xodigital syntheses + a16z §2.1 + don-techno cross_industry_ideas (numbered episodic series)
rows.lesson: Named, repeatable series may make an account recognisable: fixed chrome and skeleton, changing content, a numbered cover. Whether they win is unmeasured, so series are an experiment. Pinning the client's own visual system is a brand-fidelity matter handled elsewhere.
rows.scope: all clients as an experiment
rows.mechanism: A series has a fixed skeleton (slot order, cover grammar, closer) and a number on its cover. Content changes each edition, the chrome does not.
rows.value: Per DNA: series names, skeletons, numbering on or off.
rows.evidence: Anecdotal winners: @reputeforge repeats one module 8x (19.18x), @viralnation 17.97x, Me Poupe 15 slides in one layout (28.35x), Corner's identical end-to-end skeleton, two mindtrip templates behind all 5 of its best carousels, a16z's ~17 templates under one system, and housemusic.us's 'Nostalgic House #n' (the only reels in its best set). L1-14 was killed: there is no within-account statistic, the evidence has survivorship bias, and winners' posts show 2-3 bits of layout entropy (they mix layouts across posts). Fatigue runs the other way: a16z explainers fell 1.0 → 0.46x.

rows.source: research (Buffer 2M+ posts/~100K accounts; Eden 655K carousels) + storm lead param 'Cadence and dedupe' + a16z §2.8 + kindlyyours synthesis + thepitchbydeel L2 + don-techno cross_industry_ideas (empty slot, fallback ladder)
rows.lesson: Plan at least 3 feed posts a week per client, but the floor is a target, not a gate. When nothing clears the bar, deliver from a fallback ladder and say which rung was used, never a generic filler. Interleaving formats is practice, not a measured lever.
rows.scope: all clients; the per-week value is a DNA param
rows.mechanism: The planner fills weekly slots to postsPerWeek. When the topic door finds nothing, it falls down a ladder (current hit → anniversary/comeback → benchmark subject with fresh material → declared industry, flagged) and records the rung. Format interleaving is a TRY toggle.
rows.value: postsPerWeek per DNA (default 3-5). Per-format quotas. interleave=TRY.
rows.evidence: Buffer: 3-5 feed posts a week about doubles follower growth compared with less, with further gains at 6-9. Eden: 3+ carousels a week reach 2x the creator median 30.1% of the time vs 22-24%. Both are large samples, but correlational. Practice: a16z 4.98/week, weekdays, formats interleaved. Kindly's peers post 2.9-4/week, while Kindly has been silent since 2026-08-31. Music competitors post a median 15.8/week. DT's old automated pipeline fell to 0.2 posts a week. DT's rule: 'an empty slot is a good result; a weak post is not'. Interleaving has no test.

rows.source: storm lead param 'Cadence and dedupe' + don-techno dedupe study (1,074 posts) + a16z §5.1.9 + thepitchbydeel L2 (500global, join_ef) + kindlyyours synthesis (OEAK, third reel) + research (Meta originality rule)
rows.lesson: Repeats are governed at three levels: the same asset never; the same storyline and the same entity or guest only after a rest window measured on the client's own grid; and any hook, ask or offer formula at most twice before it rests.
rows.scope: all clients; windows per client
rows.mechanism: 07d replaces the single text-similarity check (evaluateDedupe, 0.4) with three keyed checks: asset hash (never; MUST), storyline key (window), entity key (window). There is also a formula counter for hooks, asks and offer templates. Windows are computed from the client's own repeats once n is enough, otherwise the default.
rows.value: Default storyline 30 d, entity 3 d, formula ≤2 uses per 4 weeks, and never two of the same guest or format in one week. DT measured: storyline 60 d, entity 2 d.
rows.evidence: DT own page (1,074 posts): a reposted clip always did worse (0.04-0.55x). The same storyline within 60 days did 0.84x (n=32), after 60 days 1.33x (n=42). The same artist 1-2 days later did 0.67x (n=66), 3-7 days later 1.17x (n=99). The measured rules block 117 of 957 posts vs 395 under the old guess. On news pages a same-storyline follow-up within 30 days did not suffer (1.09x, n=103), so the windows are per client. Elsewhere: a16z 3 Brockman posts in 4 days 0.14-0.42x; 500global repeated flyer 0.10-0.28x and triple clip 0.08-0.24x; join_ef repeated roundup 0.18/0.33x; OEAK keyword ask 8.5x → 0.5x in weeks; Kindly's third 'perfect day' reel got 239 views. Asset reuse is also an originality risk under the April 2026 rule.

extent.note: Defaults. Near-duplicate posts compete with each other (reputeforge's recycled Braun/iPod post 0.28x).
Storyline window short or off for follow-ups (news pages 1.09x within 30 d). Entity window only for the same product.
Never cut one conversation into back-to-back clips. The same judge or guest never twice in a week. Never re-post a flyer.
The keyword-DM ask at most once a week, only on a named style with a fresh reason. Any reel formula reused at most twice.
The venue is the entity: a spot never appears twice within the window across series.
The offer template never twice in a week. The capybara at most once per carousel.
Keep the measured 60 d / 2 d and same-clip-never.
The property itself is exempt from the entity window (every post is N°3). Windows apply per apartment and theme, and the asset-never rule binds hardest given the small library.

rows.agent_change: 07d gains asset/storyline/entity/formula keys. A config dedupe block in the DNA (from DT's config/dedupe.yaml shape). The weekly own-grid job computes the windows. Asset-never is a code gate with a fixture (MUST). Windows are tuning params.

rows.source: storm L1-04 (survived) + L1-03 (killed, register part) + scale.md hook_type rows (all/industry) + a16z §5.2 + geektime/karoslabs/thepitchbydeel/xodigital/sitti syntheses + don-techno cross_industry_ideas (chore posts)
rows.lesson: Topic mix: posts about a named outside subject (a person, a company, a place, a news event with a reader stake, a story) beat the brand's own promotion, generic how-to and chore posts (link digests, repeated flyers, logistics reminders, routine firm news). Promotion keeps a capped slot and must carry a hook: a date, a price, a free thing or a named person.
rows.scope: all clients; promo share and the definition of 'news' per kit
rows.mechanism: 03f-rank-topic-candidates applies topic-kind priors (external named subject / news-with-stake / story ↑; house promo / offer / how-to / chore ↓). A promo slot quota. A promo candidate without a hook field fails the door.
rows.value: Kit/DNA postModes weights and promoShare (e.g. retail 0.2-0.25, B2B/media 0.1). The chore list per kit.
rows.evidence: Within accounts (all 183): story/narrative +0.10 (74+/28-, p<0.001); news/announcement +0.06 (74+/45-, p=0.01); product promo/offer -0.08 (31+/50-, p=0.045); how-to/guide -0.09 (27+/47-, p=0.026). Promo is negative in most industries: B2B -0.17 (0+/2-), intimates -0.06, fintech -0.08 (0+/3-), Hebrew news -0.17 (0+/4-), creator -0.29 (1+/3-). It is neutral in startup (0.00) and luxury (+0.01, 4+/6-), and slightly positive in BR fintech (+0.03, 4+/2-), so no single industry drives it. News is positive except startup (-0.13, 3+/6-) and music (-0.06, 1+/5-), where 'news' is the account's own programme or lineup posts. Examples: Calcalist house promo 0.09x, WIRED 0.07x, VisualCap partner posts 10/10 below median, a16z routine firm news 0.24-1.16x and talking-head promos 0.19x, Karos peers' internal posts weakest, Nath own-product pitches 5 of 6 worst, repeated flyers 0.10-0.33x. Caveats: tags double as hook labels, there is no multiple-comparison correction, and hidden likes contaminate the weakest sets.

extent.note: The subject is a famous brand or campaign with a live peg. 1 in 3 posts from Karos-owned work (the output, not the pitch).
News with an Israeli stake (price, date, availability, named person). House programmes and partner content never run as news. No how-to (0+/4-).
The founder is the hero and Deel is never the subject. Programme news only as a big launch with partner co-posts. One offer a week.
Occasion, person or participation first. Product explanation and seasonal taglines underperform (0.67-0.74). Offers allowed with a named pack and price in the caption.
Creator first-person over brand feature copy. Launch-weighted promo (Amazon) allowed within the quota.
A named place, person or city plus a concrete promise. Never 'monetise your recommendations' pitches (0.15-0.23x).
A rule-change explainer with a date counts as news with a stake, not how-to. Hard-sell only on a hook. Proposals labelled as not in force.
Ticket and lineup posts average 1.09x. Cap logistics posts and fold reminders into stories.
Luxury promo is neutral, not negative. Lead with place, story and behind-the-scenes (+0.17, 10+/3-; +0.10). Availability and TTC price only as the caption's fact, never a sales plate.

rows.source: don-techno synthesis (doors; market ≠ own audience) + robustness-v2 + taxonomy judge + storm L1-17 (survived)
rows.lesson: A subject enters the plan only with a measured reason: an outlier for its own account, a sweet spot in the client's own history, a dated researched story with a primary source, an external chart, or a client hand-in. rows.source: ranking research (Meta 30 Apr 2026 originality rule, Mosseri); storm L1-21 (survived); Don Techno audit (rights model); a16z deep dive (endorsement risk)
rows.lesson: Third-party media (press photos, archival images, screenshots, UGC, footage) may appear only with a credit and a material edit (our own type and layout), and a deck, or a client's feed over 30 days, must never be mostly third-party media.
rows.scope: all clients; every third-party frame and the account over time
rows.evidence: On 30 Apr 2026 Meta extended its unoriginal-content rules to photos and carousels. Accounts that mostly post content they did not create or materially edit lose recommendation to non-followers, and the penalty applies to all their posts. Watermarks, crops, credits, borders or a new caption don't count as edits. DT's rights model is an aggregator norm (credit line, pull the post on a DMCA notice), which its own audit says doesn't carry over to brand clients; check_copy.py fails a caption without a Video:/Photo:/Via line. a16z posts famous founders' archival images, but The Pitch is a Deel property and must not imply endorsement. Our runs: Google Places photos with no credit; a Wikimedia logo as a picture; XO's CVM logo with a CC BY string on the slide.
rows.mechanism: A provenance record per frame (tier, licence, credit, edited yes/no). A gate on thirdPartyShare per deck, a credit line in the caption for every third-party frame, and an account-level 30-day monitor. A likeness rule: a real person's image never implies endorsement unless the person is officially involved.

rows.lesson: Picture quality is measured in code before any model judges a picture: resolution, upscale limit, brightness and contrast, no other page's watermark or burned-in text over the subject, no ad, no AI label on third-party media.
rows.scope: all clients; every sourced photo and video frame
rows.evidence: DT's flat gates are stored as data: first-2-second YAVG at least 20, median brightness at least 55, contrast at least 28, 720p on the best rendition, crop plus scale at most 1.5x for clean sources and 1.1x for soft ones, no burned-in text over the subject, no other page's watermark, not an ad, an AI-label check. 'Every traced winner used bright, real footage.' 6am_group's weakest include the darkest, least legible covers in the sample. Music: bright/saturated designed colour 0+/6-, while colour from footage wins. Hanky Panky's best covers have a median 64% vivid pixels vs 39% for the weakest. Our engine: Google Places returns a photo for any name, and the vet is a model judgement with no measured floor.
rows.mechanism: A code pre-vet (sharp/ffmpeg) measures the short edge (at least 1440 px for the 1080x1440 canvas), the upscale factor, brightness and contrast floors, watermark and sticker detection, and third-party AI labels, before the image vet runs. Failing frames are dropped, never repaired by generation.

rows.scope: all clients

Thin weights lose glance legibility and fail under JPEG re-encode (Dobres/Reimer 2016). Our runs shipped 15, 16 and 22px lines; the Karos archive has a 19px credit and a 23px eyebrow. Owner C asked for bigger reading text (drift review: the T floor is 44px against today's 32px). This is legibility, not a performance lever: headline_size=huge is null at 183 accounts (46+/35-, p=0.27).

rows.source: owner H; storm L1-08 (survived) and L1-19 (only its contrast part survived); scale.md text_contrast; a16z 2.3 and 4.5; research:karos-archive; research:legibility; audit:typography-layout
rows.lesson: Every text box on a photo or busy ground sits on a measured legibility device (a scrim, a card or plate, or a naturally dark area). Contrast is measured against the worst pixels under the box and must reach 4.5:1 (3:1 at 72px and up). Brand text/ground colour pairs that fail are banned at kit load.
rows.scope: all clients, all text on photos or designed grounds, and marks
rows.evidence: text_contrast=medium -0.14 over 111 accounts (24+/72-, p<0.0001), negative in 7 of 9 industries (Hebrew 0+/8- p=0.008, fintech & investing 3+/11-, B2B 1+/6-, Brazil 2+/7-, music 1+/4-, luxury 1+/4-, startup 4+/5-) and near-null in creator (2+/3-) and intimates (4+/2-). High contrast +0.06 over 160 (71+/41-, p=0.006); Hebrew 6+/0-. a16z: median background behind text is 7-34/255, against 71 on our Pitch cover. Karos archive: the orange eyebrow falls under 3:1 on 29 of 54 photo slides, the wordmark on 17. NN/g: a 30% overlay is too weak, 50%+ is needed. WCAG: black at 0.54 opacity gives 4.5:1 over white. #FF6B2C on white is 2.84:1. DT: always-on gradient, clear above 42%, 225/255 at the edge. Where our failures come from: #230 set .scrim display:none; even restored, the scrim has fixed stops and is clear above 62% with a flat 0.22 veil; Sitti's cover got a light cream fade under white text; the top third of photo slides has no scrim, so the logo sits on unmeasured pixels.
rows.mechanism: CONTRAST gate on the rendered file: for each line box, compare the p10/worst-5% background against the text colour (4.5:1 below 72px or 56px bold, 3:1 above). The scrim is anchored one line above the measured copy. A top micro-veil protects the mark when the top 15% is bright. At kit load, every text/ground pair gets a WCAG and APCA check and failing pairs are banned by size.

rows.source: research:karos-archive (owner 'too empty' rounds of 6 Jul v2, 6 Jul v3 and 28 Jul); audit:typography-layout (dead-space remedy)
rows.lesson: A plate slide should not leave a large empty band. The copy block and the device or image form one column, with the element as the elastic middle. Empty bands taller than about 26% of the height fail, except on deliberately sparse slides. The fix changes the object or layout, never the type size.
rows.scope: designed plate slides (not photo-led or wordless slides)
rows.evidence: Karos archive: 22 of 63 flat slides (35%) in the 6-8 Jul batches carried an empty band of 380px or more. The owner flagged 'too blank / too empty' in three separate rounds. The fit.mjs DEAD-SPACE gate (380px, 26% of 1440) cut this to 4 of 64. There is no cross-account statistic. In the engine, the interest-relayout dead-space remedy changes per-slide fontScale (interest-relayout.ts:1101-1109), which creates off-scale sizes and conflicts with DS-02.
rows.mechanism: DEAD-SPACE gate on the rendered file, with remedies: grow the object or photo, reassign the layout, or fold the words into the caption. No font rescale.
rows.value: Threshold about 26% of height; a sparse-slide exemption flag per layout.

rows.source: owner C (complete, human, non-AI sentences); owner N3 rule 2026-09-08/09 (complete French sentences, a fact per slide, plain words); DT content-spec 3.5 plain voice (Albert 2026-09-22); storm L1-05 (survived, 1 refutation)

The performance data backs the anti-fragment half but not a 'complete sentences win' claim. Across all accounts, sentence_form=complete sentences is null (+0.02, 61+/59-, p=0.93, n=152). Luxury reverses when text sits on the image (-0.20, 0+/6-, p=0.031), which argues for fewer words, not worse ones. rows.source: owner C; storm L1-05; audit:copy-language; don-techno (check_copy.py + copy_rules.yaml); research:karos-archive; client syntheses (7 of 7 gap reports)
rows.lesson: No AI-tell rhetoric. This means no 'X is not A. It is B.' or 'Not X.' frames (at most one ', not X' tail per post), no stacks of three or more short fragments, no teasers that never resolve, no aphorisms or rhetorical triads, and no meta lines about the post.
rows.scope: all clients, all rendered text plus the caption, in every locale
rows.mechanism: A deterministic lint that uses no model (readable-copy 07h3) over the assembled slides and the caption. It refuses on attempts 1 to n-1 and blocks on the final attempt. Pattern packs are keyed by script.
rows.value: Per-locale pattern packs (en, he 'לא X.', pt 'não X, mas Y', fr 'ne ... pas X, mais Y' and two-word flourishes), plus each client's own banned list in its DNA.
rows.evidence: Owner point C calls this 'sounds like AI'. Performance agrees at platform scale. sentence_form=fragments/labels scores -0.07 over 162 accounts (48+/83-, sign p=0.0028). It holds with any one industry left out (p between 0.001 and 0.007 each time), holds in every involvement band (high 19+/32-, low 16+/29-, none 13+/23-), and leans the same way in the enrichment verticals that exclude all client industries (15+/27-, p=0.088). The 51-post audit found a 'Not X.' fragment in 19 posts and runs of three or more sentences of 4 words or fewer in 11. The Karos archive has 12 of 151 headlines that are 'X, not Y' antitheses. On DT, 32 of 36 builders shared one fragment rhythm, and check_copy.py failed 26 of 41 old builders on day one. Same-clip first lines: a named line scored 2.95 and a vague aphorism 0.35.

No 'not X, it's Y' aphorisms and no em dashes (lab voice).

rows.lesson: The hook names a real subject (a person, product, place, event or number) and tells what happened to it or what changes for the reader, as a story. Abstract advice, how-to or framework hooks and the brand's own promotion lose unless they carry a reader stake: a date, a price, a free thing or a named person.

rows.evidence: hook_type=story/narrative scores +0.10 over 124 accounts (74+/28-, p<0.0001). It is null in B2B (1+/2-) and tech news (3+/4-), where the lever is the stake, not the narrative. how-to/guide scores -0.09 (27+/47-, p=0.027), with enrichment-only 5+/22- (p=0.002), publishers 2+/12- (p=0.013) and low involvement 7+/20-. It is neutral at high involvement (14+/17-), in B2B (5+/4-) and in fintech (3+/3-). product promo/offer scores -0.08 (31+/50-, p=0.045), with publishers 0+/12- (p<0.001). Primary examples: a16z's 13 of 17 outliers centre a famous founder or company, and reference or explainer posts went 0 for 12 at 2x. Geektime's same iPhone topic ran 12.3x with an Israeli price or date and 0.75x without (n=4 vs 5). Techstars aphorisms 0.36-0.51x vs 8.4x for a named founder. The DT same clip: a named person and moment scored 2.95, a vague line 0.35. Confound: famous subjects and Collabs travel with story hooks. rows.lesson: Register: hype and promotional copy loses almost everywhere, a personal or human register wins, and flat informational copy loses. Which positive register fits depends on the audience: conversational for B2B and high-involvement, emotional/personal or creator first-person for low-involvement consumer brands, and plain authoritative for publishers and scene media.

rows.evidence: hype/promotional scores -0.12 over 111 accounts (27+/68-, p<0.0001). It holds with any one industry left out (all p≤0.001), and the enrichment verticals alone show 8+/19- (p=0.052). It is strongest for publishers (2+/21-), person accounts (1+/10-), no-involvement accounts (2+/24-), music (0+/7-, p=0.016) and luxury (1+/6-). It is weak for brands (9+/13-) and B2B audiences (7+/9-), and null in intimates (6+/6-). emotional/personal scores +0.12 (66+/27-, p=0.0001), holds with any industry left out (all p<0.001), and shows enrichment-only 23+/9- (p=0.020). It is null in Brazil fintech (1+/4-). neutral/informational scores -0.08 (27+/62-, p=0.0003), with enrichment-only 7+/20- (p=0.019) and B2B audience 3+/12- (p=0.035). conversational is null overall (70+/56-) but wins for B2B audiences (15+/5-, p=0.041), high involvement (33+/16-, p=0.021) and B2B marketing (7+/1-). authoritative/expert is null overall but wins for publishers (19+/6-, p=0.015) and music (7+/0-, p=0.016). Karos synthesis: conversational lift 2.15, informational 0.47, hype 0.5. Confound: register tracks topic (promotional posts lose on topic), so this is a default, not a classifier gate.

rows.lesson: Every post carries a hook. When the cover is wordless (a photo-led or product frame), the caption's first line carries it. In the enrichment verticals alone it is directional (2+/8-, p=0.11). transfers.pattern: Photo-dominant colour: the photograph sets the post's colour, with no designed plate or wash, and saturated real colour is never desaturated
transfers.source_evidence: Luxury: +0.50 within-account, 10 accounts, 10+/0-, p=0.002, the strongest single result in the study. Tech news repeats it (+0.27, 10+/1-, p=0.012), and so do all 183 accounts (+0.21, 99+/26-). Muted/neutral loses in luxury (-0.21) and across the board (35+/92-). Target: only 13.6% of intimate-apparel posts are photo-dominant, and the target is not contradicted: +0.125 over 12 accounts (8+/4-); kindlyyours +0.214 (5+/2-), hankypanky +0.056 (4+/2-).
transfers.target: Intimate apparel: Hanky Panky and Kindly Yours
transfers.twist: Luxury gets its colour from rooms and light. In lingerie the colour has to come from the product colourway on real bodies in real rooms: saturated Signature Lace shades on candid, laughing women, with the colourway setting the palette (B2B's brand-colour-heavy result, 5+/1-, which is +0.222 3+/0- at Hanky Panky, points the same way). Keep the luxury grammar: no text on the photo, no plates, no logo on photos, every slide a new picture, angle or body, and close on the clearest product-visible frame. Never borrow the beige-interior palette, never desaturate (vivid pixels: 64% of best posts vs 39% of weakest), no stock, no AI. Fonts and logo stay the brand kit's (Relais Display/Fabriga for Hanky Panky).
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Both are high-involvement categories that sell a sensory promise the viewer judges by eye. A frame that reads as a real photograph stops the scroll and survives Instagram's 2026 originality and authenticity push, while a designed card reads as an ad. The effect holds in 10 of 10 luxury accounts and in 99 of 125 signed accounts overall. It is an audience-level visual response, not a luxury-specific topic, which matches the grouping test ranking involvement above industry.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 in both DNAs. Posts: the client's experiment slot (every 10th scheduled run), 3 posts per client, randomising only the colour/visual dimension: an all-photo, zero-plate carousel of 3-7 slides against the client's current designed-card mix on similar product topics. Metric: likes + 3×comments as a multiple of the client's own median, read at 7 days, skipping posts under 72h; for Kindly Yours (likes hidden on @teamkindly) use Insights saves and sends per reach. Window: 30-day TRY review. Success bar: at least 2 of 3 experiment posts at or above the client's 7-day median promotes the line to DEFAULT. If both clients pass, raise an L2 kit proposal for apparel-intimates. Kindly Yours runs only after its client record is fixed (it currently generates wedding-gift content).
transfers.risk: Photo-dominant co-occurs with famous subjects and Collab/creator posts (a data caveat), so part of the luxury lift may be borrowed reach. Needs real shoot supply: without owned photography the engine falls back to stock/AI, which loses (stock 11+/25- on all accounts). Kindly Yours' broken client record blocks it until fixed.

transfers.pattern: News cover built on the object itself: a real photo of the product or document, shot or held, carrying a checkable stake (price, date, rule)
transfers.source_evidence: Tech news: photo-dominant +0.27, 11 accounts, 10+/1-, p=0.012; real product/object photo +0.24, 5+/1-; news with a stake 8+/2-. Geektime's own product-in-hand price posts: 26.5x, 16.11x, 8.54x. Target fintech: photo-dominant in 14.6% of leader posts and 9.3% of Brazil-peer posts. Not contradicted: +0.131 over 14 accounts (9+/4-) among leaders, +0.121 (5+/4-) among Brazil peers; product/object +0.146 over 8 among leaders. Stock photos lose among fintech leaders (0+/6-, p=0.031) and at XO (1+/4-). Closest in-market proof: @nathfinancas' law explainers with a card machine or real price tags on the cover (31.5x, 26.75x).
transfers.twist: The 'product' in regulated investing is a document, a rule or a price, not a gadget. Photograph the actual thing (the offer's asset, the real price tag, the card machine, the printed CVM resolution) under a scrim. Put the stake as one complete pt-BR sentence in XO's condensed display face with a date. Every regulatory claim carries a status badge in XO's style ('PROPOSTA DA CVM · AINDA NÃO ESTÁ EM VIGOR'), plus a 'Mas atenção' slide. Never use the regulator's logo as decoration. Freshness gate as at Geektime: lead fact at most 7 days old, or dated on the slide.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Both audiences scroll for news that changes something they can act on. A photographed object turns an abstract change into something recognisable in the thumbnail and reads as reporting, not an ad. That is why stock loses in both industries and why the same cover form tops Brazilian personal-finance media. XO's rule-change explainer is the same job as a tech-news price-and-availability post.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-xodigital). Posts: 3 rule-change or offer explainers in XO's experiment slot, randomising only the cover's visual source (object photo vs XO's current brand plate). Metric: saves + sends per reach from Insights (XO has 385 followers and carousels flat at 5-18 likes, so the like multiple can't rank designs), plus a blind side-by-side reviewer check against the compliance gate. Window: 30 days. Success bar: every experiment post passes the compliance gate, and 2 of 3 are at or above XO's 7-day median saves+sends per reach; otherwise the line retires at review.
transfers.risk: Photo supply: XO needs owned or licensed photos of real objects or documents, and stock or AI stand-ins would reverse the effect. Compliance: a photographed document can read as endorsement, and a proposal must never appear as a rule in force. The Brazil-peer cohort alone is only 5+/4-, so the target evidence leans on the leader cohort.

transfers.pattern: One text size per slide: a single sentence at a single size, with emphasis carried by one accent device rather than a size step
transfers.source_evidence: Luxury: one distinct text size +0.17 within-account, 9 accounts, 7+/1-, p=0.07. All 183 accounts: one size +0.05 (63+/41-, p=0.039), 4+ sizes -0.11 (16+/43-, p=0.0006), 3 sizes -0.07 (32+/56-). Target B2B: one-size posts are 14.7% of the industry's posts; not contradicted and already positive, +0.146 over 8 accounts (6+/1-). a16z's winners use one short serif line per slide at one size. Our Karos runs used 7-14 type sizes.
transfers.target: B2B marketing / AI agency: Karos Labs
transfers.twist: Luxury achieves one size by having almost no words. Karos is an ideas brand and needs sentences, so the rule becomes one sentence per slide at one size: Spectral Medium at the kit's interior size (64-72px), with the orange block in Spectral Medium Italic as the only emphasis and no size step. Tracked DM Mono eyebrows stay as the one permitted small label. Display numbers stay serif at the same size as the line they sit in. Allow at most one 'receipt' slide per carousel (a real asset or side-by-side comparison, B2B's own 4+/1- winner) that may carry a second size. No boxes, pills or icons as containers, since those are Karos's biggest measured liability (boxes 2+/7-).
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: This is a legibility mechanism, not an aesthetic one. One size forces one idea per slide, reads at phone size, and gives Meta's swipe-completion and dwell predictions a reason to continue instead of a wall to skip. It holds across all accounts, so it is close to platform-level. Luxury and a16z show it survives in premium registers, which is the register Karos's editorial serif grid is aiming for.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-karoslabs), with a Watching entry at the marketing-services kit. Posts: 3 carousels in Karos's experiment slot, randomising only the type-scale dimension (one size per slide vs the current kit scale), with the same topic class (named brand, person or number) on both arms. Metric: Karos has no usable baseline (22 followers, median 3 likes), so month one is judged by the reviewer and owner against the lettered brief, with a measured type audit (sizes per slide ≤2, words per slide ≤25). Performance is tracked as sends/saves per reach once the account has a baseline. Window: 30 days. Success bar: all 3 pass the type audit, the owner approves 2 of 3 over the control, and there are no lost-word or cut-off defects. Then promote to DEFAULT and propose it at L2.
transfers.risk: The luxury source is 9 accounts at p=0.07 and the target is 8 accounts, so this rests mainly on the all-account result. A one-size rule collides with dense explainers, so the word cap must follow from the minimum size or the renderer will shrink text. Needs the renderer to enforce one scale (currently a WS-level defect, not a prompt fix).

transfers.pattern: Story hook with one named real person and one real number on the cover, then a fixed beat structure (setup, turn, proof)
transfers.source_evidence: Creator economy: story/narrative hook +0.25, 8 accounts, 6+/1-. Stan's named-creator story (Nina's $45 Japan guide, '$85,235 in two weeks') reached 23.0x and its sequel 17.0x, while the same idea told as generic advice scored 0.23x. Replicated in luxury (10+/3-), intimate apparel (10+/1-, p=0.012) and all 183 accounts (74+/28-, p<0.0001). Target: story hooks are 6.9% of Brazil-fintech posts. Not contradicted: +0.056 over 6 (3+/1-) in the Brazil cohort, +0.148 over 9 among leaders.
transfers.twist: In a CVM-regulated investing platform, the named person can't be a returns testimonial. The story is a real, consenting investor's (or issuer's) decision and constraint: why a named small business raised through XO, or how one investor worked out their R$ 20 mil annual limit across platforms. The number is a checkable fact (amount raised, limit, date), never a return or a promise. Complete conversational pt-BR sentences, the catch before the reassurance, and the disclaimer and registration line in the caption. The beat structure stays fixed: person and number on the cover, the turn, the document or proof, the rule, the CTA only on the current rule.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A named person with a stake opens a loop the viewer swipes to close. That feeds Meta's carousel-completion prediction, and it turns an abstract rule into identification, which is what fintech leaders already reward (emotional register 7+/2-). The mechanism is audience psychology rather than topic, so it has held in every industry tested except B2B and Hebrew tech news, where it is flat.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-xodigital). Posts: 3 in XO's experiment slot after X2's, randomising only the hook dimension (named-person story vs XO's current rule or offer headline), with topics drawn from real XO offers where the person has consented. Metric: sends and saves per reach and swipe-through (Insights) at 7 days, since likes can't rank designs on a 385-follower account. Window: 30-45 days (shares the slot with X2 and X10). Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above XO's 7-day median on sends+saves per reach, with zero compliance-gate failures.
transfers.risk: Consent and compliance: a named investor story drifts easily into implied returns, which a CVM-authorised platform cannot publish. Source evidence is 8 accounts at p=0.125, and story hooks co-occur with famous or creator-authored posts. It needs real people willing to be named.

transfers.pattern: Emotional/personal register: the post carries a person's own stake and feeling in the first person
transfers.source_industry: Fintech & investing (category leaders), replicated in music media and creator economy
transfers.source_evidence: Fintech leaders: +0.28 within-account, 9 accounts, 7+/2-. Music 6+/1-, creator economy 5+/0- (p=0.06), all 183 accounts +0.12 (66+/27-, p=0.0001). Target: emotional register is 9% of Hebrew tech-news posts; not contradicted, +0.167 over 5 accounts (3+/1-). TheMarker, the best Hebrew business carousel craft in the set, leads covers with a person's quote.
transfers.twist: Geektime's own voice stays dry news. The emotion belongs to a named person, quoted in their own Hebrew words on the cover (founder, engineer, laid-off developer, reader), attached to a real news stake and within the 7-day freshness gate. Actor + verb + consequence, 5-9 words plus the quote. No open questions (5.6% of best vs 13.9% of weakest), no how-to, and no Geektime house programme dressed as a personal story. Wordmark right of centre on the plate for right-to-left layout.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Readers of tech news share stories about people more than announcements about companies. A quoted human stake gives a send trigger ('look what this founder said') on top of the news value. The register effect is one of the most general in the study (66 of 93 signed accounts) and does not depend on topic.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-geektime). Posts: 3 news posts in Geektime's experiment slot, randomising only the register dimension (named-person quote cover vs Geektime's standard news headline plate) on comparable stories. Metric: likes + 3×comments as a multiple of Geektime's own median, read at 24-48h (the kit's news measurement window) and confirmed at 7 days, plus sends per reach. Window: 30 days. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above Geektime's 7-day median.
transfers.risk: Target evidence is only 5 accounts, and the source signal is p=0.18 in its own industry. A quote can smuggle in stale news or a partner's PR line, so the freshness gate and the no-house-programme rule must stay in force.

transfers.pattern: Emotional/personal register: first-person stake from a named person
transfers.source_industry: Fintech & investing (category leaders), replicated in music media and creator economy
transfers.source_evidence: Fintech leaders +0.28 (7+/2-), music 6+/1-, creator economy 5+/0-, all accounts 66+/27- (p=0.0001). Target: 12.8% of startup-program posts; not contradicted, +0.111 over 9 accounts (5+/3-). a16z: 13 of 17 outliers are built around a named founder or company.
transfers.target: Startup / founder programs: The Pitch by Deel
transfers.twist: The emotional moment is a real founder's, in their words, around the act of pitching: the night before the stage, the first 'no', the question from a judge they still think about. It goes on a real event or backstage photo with a scrim, Inter 400 headline at one size, no condensed caps (0+/9-), no devices, and a small watermark logo. Never invent how The Pitch judges, never use Deel parent branding, and Collab the post with the founder (1.38x vs 0.85x in the kit).
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Founder audiences identify with other founders' vulnerability more than with programme announcements (news hooks lean negative here, 3+/6-). A first-person moment is also what makes an event recap shareable to a co-founder. It pairs with the industry's proven recognition mechanism without needing a famous name.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-thepitchbydeel). Posts: 3 in the experiment slot, randomising only the register (founder first-person moment vs the current informational recap), as Collabs where the founder agrees. Metric: likes are hidden on all @deelpitch posts, so use reel views or carousel reach and sends+saves per reach from Insights, at 7 days. Window: 30 days. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above the account's 7-day median views/reach.
transfers.risk: The Pitch client's own signal is only 5+/3-. Hidden likes mean no public baseline. It needs founders' consent and real quotes; a model-written 'founder feeling' would be fabricated and must be blocked.

transfers.pattern: Wordless photo sequence: no sentence on the slides, the pictures carry the post, and names and context go in the caption
transfers.source_evidence: Luxury: sentence_form=none +0.24 within-account, 7 accounts, 5+/1-; one text size 7+/1-; devices almost absent. Music repeats 'no type on image' (font none 4+/0-). Target: 7.1% of startup posts are wordless. Not contradicted: +0.125 over 4 accounts (2+/1-), and the industry's own adjacent signals point the same way: devices none +0.36 (8+/0-, p=0.008), font none +0.20 (3+/0-), headline none +0.19 (4+/1-). a16z's biggest post (Roblox archive, 60.5x) has no added type, and @speedrun's best are documentary cohort photos.
transfers.target: Startup / founder programs: The Pitch by Deel
transfers.twist: Luxury shows rooms. The Pitch shows people inside its own events: stage, backstage, judges mid-question, founders' hands on the clicker, and the room after. The cover may carry only a small event-name and date label in Inter 500, with no sentence. Captions carry the names and a declarative first line (300-450 characters). Real photos only (0 AI, 0 stock) and a small watermark logo. Use for event recaps and behind-the-scenes posts, never for offers.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Documentary photos read as insider access and proof that the event is real, which is what recaps are for. Instagram's 2026 push toward raw, original media rewards exactly that, and removing text removes the part our engine gets wrong most often (wrong fonts, retired brand). Premium audiences in both industries respond to quiet confidence over explanation.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-thepitchbydeel). Posts: 3 event or backstage recaps in the experiment slot, randomising only the text-on-slide dimension (wordless vs the current headline-per-slide recap), with the same event photos available to both arms. Metric: carousel reach, sends and saves per reach from Insights at 7 days (likes hidden). Window: 30 days, timed to the event calendar. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above the account's 7-day median reach.
transfers.risk: Target evidence is only 4 accounts. It depends entirely on a supply of good event photography. Wordless posts give OCR and search no topic keywords, so the caption's first line must carry the event and names.

transfers.pattern: Long caption (over 600 characters) that tells the story behind one named thing
transfers.source_evidence: Music: +0.29 within-account, 7 accounts, 6+/0-, p=0.031, carried by story-behind-a-record posts (3.5x). The Brazil fintech peers repeat it (8+/3-), and so do all accounts (+0.08, 76+/37-, p=0.0003). Target: long captions are 4.8% of intimate-apparel posts. Not contradicted: +0.229 over 8 accounts (8+/0-, p=0.008); short captions lose (1+/12-, p=0.003); hankypanky +0.278 (3+/0-), kindlyyours +0.194 (6+/0-). Platform: captions are indexed by Google since July 2025, and 400+ character captions reach 2x median more often (28.5% vs 25.4%, Eden).
transfers.target: Intimate apparel: Hanky Panky (then Kindly Yours)
transfers.twist: Music's long caption is the story behind a record. Lingerie's is the story behind one named style: who designed it, how the lace is made, the fit problem it solved, and one real customer's words. It is written in a witty first-person creator voice (emotional register 9+/2- in the industry), 600-900 characters, with a searchable first line naming the style and category, and it ends on one answerable question. On-image copy stays at 0-10 words, so the caption carries the words, not the slides. No contest or giveaway rules count toward the test.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A long caption adds dwell time and search surface without adding text to the photo, and a named origin story gives fans something to save and send. It is the same mechanism that makes music's anniversary stories outperform. Lingerie buyers research fit and fabric, so a real story about one style answers a purchase question rather than padding.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-hankypanky), then Kindly Yours once its record is fixed. Posts: 3 in the experiment slot, randomising only caption length and form (600-900 character story vs the kit's short one-liner) on similar photo posts, excluding giveaways and contests. Metric: likes + 3×comments multiple vs Hanky Panky's own median at 7 days, plus saves per reach. Window: 30 days. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above the client's 7-day median; otherwise it stays with the kit's short-caption default.
transfers.risk: The in-industry long-caption lift is confounded by giveaway and contest rules (Aerie 9,855 comments), and the lead kit currently recommends short captions (27-155 character medians), so this needs an explicit owner call if it conflicts. It needs true product facts; invented heritage copy is a fabrication risk.

transfers.pattern: Side-by-side comparison hook, readable in a second, turned into a finite-choice question
transfers.source_evidence: B2B: comparison hook +0.19 within-account, 6 accounts, 4+/1-. @reputeforge colours-vs-shades 19.18x (87.6k likes), logo-vs-branding 8.83x; a16z's 2-slide before/after 9.5x. Target: comparisons are 2.6% of intimate-apparel posts. Not contradicted: +0.067 over 5 accounts; kindlyyours +0.125 (3+/1-). Closest in-category proof: @oeak_official's 'Which team are you on?' A-D card got 118 likes against 7 for a statement card on the same template.
transfers.twist: B2B compares brands and assets. For a mass-price wireless bra brand, compare fits, feels or styles on real product cut-outs or real bodies (wireless vs underwire, two colourways, two necklines), and end with a finite, answerable choice ('Team A or Team B?') instead of a verdict. Use the brand's own product photos, 1-2 type sizes, and no spec-sheet infographics. Keep the ask fresh: oeak's repeated DM ask fell to 0.5-0.8x by September.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A comparison is processed in one glance and invites a low-cost judgment. Here the judgment is also a comment, which intimate-apparel audiences reward more than any other CTA (comment prompt 11+/1-, p=0.006). It swaps B2B's intellectual contrast for a personal-preference contrast, which fits a high-involvement, body-related purchase.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-kindlyyours), only after the client record is corrected to the lab profile. Posts: 3 in the experiment slot, randomising only the hook form (comparison + choice vs a product statement card) on the same product and template. Metric: comments and saves per reach (likes hidden on @teamkindly), with keyword-DM funnels excluded, at 7 days. Window: 30 days. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above the account's 7-day median comments+saves per reach.
transfers.risk: The source statistic is weak (6 accounts, p=0.375), and the strength comes from case evidence. Comment-weighted metrics inflate this kind of post. Blocked today: Kindly Yours' prep record points at a for-sale domain and generates gifting content.

transfers.pattern: One explicit, answerable comment prompt per post
transfers.source_evidence: Intimate apparel: +0.32 within-account, 12 accounts, 11+/1-, p=0.006. Creator economy 7+/1- (p=0.07), all accounts +0.10 (49+/25-, p=0.007). Target: comment prompts are 11.1% of Brazil-fintech posts. Not contradicted but thin: +0.083 over 4 accounts (2+/2-) in the Brazil cohort, +0.095 over 7 among leaders.
transfers.twist: Lingerie asks about taste. A regulated investing platform may only ask about knowledge or experience, never about a reader's finances, and never in a way that invites advice. Use a finite-choice question tied to the rule just explained ('Você sabia que o limite soma todas as plataformas? Sim ou não?'). Never use keyword-DM on an offer. Staff replies are factual and link to the rule, never personalised recommendations. Keep XO's own save/share CTA (3+/1-) on reference posts, and use the comment ask only on explainers.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A concrete, low-effort question converts passive readers into commenters and raises comment and profile-tap predictions in Feed ranking. On a 385-follower account, early comments are also the main visible social proof. The mechanism is the ask's answerability, which carries across categories.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-xodigital), last in XO's slot queue after X2 and X4. Posts: 3 explainers, randomising only the CTA (finite-choice question vs save/share line). Metric: comments per reach and sends+saves per reach at 7 days; do not use the likes + 3×comments score, which this CTA inflates by construction. Window: 45-60 days given the shared slot. Success bar: comments per reach above the account median on 2 of 3 without a drop in saves+sends per reach, and zero compliance flags in the replies.
transfers.risk: Metric inflation (engagement counts comments 3x). Engagement-bait demotion if the ask is generic. Compliance exposure in the comment thread. Target evidence is only 4 Brazil-peer accounts, split 2+/2-.

transfers.pattern: Authoritative position post: one expert verdict stated plainly, without hype
transfers.source_evidence: Music: authoritative/expert register +0.26 within-account, 7 accounts, 7+/0-, p=0.016; bold claim/opinion 5+/1-; hype 0+/7- (p=0.016); Don Techno's kit keeps one position post a week. Target: authoritative posts are 10.2% of creator-economy posts. Not contradicted: +0.111 over 6 accounts (3+/0-); bold claim +0.111 (3+/1-); hype also loses there (1+/5-).
transfers.twist: The authority is a named local creator, not Sitti. One verdict per post about a named city: '[Creator]'s three counters in Lisbon where locals order', with one real photo per named place, a neighbourhood tag, ≤8 on-photo words, and the Sitti app card or map as the only device. End with one specific comment question ('Which one did she miss?'). No platform theory and no 'monetise your recommendations' framing (0.15-0.23x).
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Audiences in both niches follow tastemakers, and a confident, specific verdict from someone credible gives the viewer something to save and something to argue with. Music pages show the expert register beats hype in every account tested, and Sitti's product is literally creators' recommendations, so the voice fits the product.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-sitti). Posts: 3 in the experiment slot, randomising only the register (named creator's verdict vs a neutral listicle of the same places). Metric: saves and sends per reach plus likes + 3×comments multiple vs Sitti's median at 7 days, dropping hidden-like posts and posts under 72h. Window: 30 days. Success bar: 2 of 3 at or above Sitti's 7-day median saves per reach.
transfers.risk: Needs real, consenting creators and real places; a model-invented 'creator' would be fabricated. Target evidence is only 6 accounts. Bold claims about named venues carry reputational risk if wrong.

transfers.pattern: One explicit, answerable comment prompt
transfers.source_evidence: Intimate apparel: +0.32 within-account, 12 accounts, 11+/1-, p=0.006. Creator economy 7+/1-, all accounts 49+/25- (p=0.007). Target: comment prompts are 3.7% of music-media posts, untested within those accounts. Don Techno's kit notes forced CTAs don't help there (14% of best vs 12% of weakest) and questions appear in 2% of top posts.
transfers.twist: Not a generic 'what do you think?'. Use a question rooted in the scene's own comment culture, asked only on story-behind-a-record anniversary posts: 'Which year did you first hear it?' or 'Name the track that closed that set.' One plain sentence at the end of the long caption, never on the slide, never as a follow or tag ask. Credit line stays mandatory.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Dance-music audiences already comment spontaneously to identify tracks and share memories. A question that asks for that specific knowledge draws on an existing behaviour rather than begging for engagement. Comments are also the only reliable signal on music pages where likes are hidden.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (Don Techno's system doc). Posts: 3 anniversary posts in the experiment slot, randomising only the closing line (scene question vs none). Metric: comments against the page's own median at comparable age, since likes are hidden on many music pages, checked at 7 days. Window: 30 days, after the first weekly analysis (27 Sep) sets a baseline. Success bar: 2 of 3 above the page's comment median with no drop in reach.
transfers.risk: Don Techno's own data points slightly against forced CTAs, and the target is untested within-account. A repeated question wears out fast (oeak's repeated ask fell to 0.5-0.8x).

transfers.pattern: One explicit, answerable comment prompt
transfers.source_evidence: Intimate apparel: +0.32 within-account, 12 accounts, 11+/1-, p=0.006. Target: comment prompts are 3.6% of luxury-hospitality posts. Not contradicted but thin: +0.167 over 3 accounts (2+/0-).
transfers.twist: The luxury register can't carry 'comment below'. The ask becomes a quiet finite choice about the place itself, written as a complete French sentence in the caption, never on the image: 'Au réveil, vous choisissez la vue sur la Saulire ou sur la forêt ?' No numerals or italics (N°3's rules), no commerce, no booking push, and it never mentions review or approval. Apartments come first: the question always refers to a real feature of one of the three apartments.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A choice about light, view or season asks the viewer to picture themselves in the apartment, which is the whole job of a residence post. It borrows lingerie's answerable-ask mechanism without the category's playful tone.
transfers.experiment: TRY at L3 (ig-dna-n3), owner-approved before the first post. Posts: 3 in the experiment slot, randomising only the closing caption line (place question vs none). Metric: comments and saves per reach at 7 days; judge comment quality by hand (real prospective guests vs emoji). Window: 30-60 days (luxury cadence is low). Success bar: 2 of 3 above the account's saves-per-reach median and no owner objection to register.
transfers.risk: Ultra-luxury buyers rarely comment publicly, so the lift may be non-buyers. The prompt may read as cheapening the brand's register. Target evidence is only 3 accounts, and the owner's copy rules for N°3 are strict.

transfers.pattern: The story behind a well-known thing, posted on its anniversary, with one documented fact most people do not know
transfers.source_industry: Music media & nightlife (supported by Startup / founder programs)
transfers.source_evidence: Music media: about 40% of 144 traced outliers on 8 media pages follow this recipe (median 3.5x). The fact comes from the Wikipedia Background or Release section, and the anniversary sets the day. Bridge posts, which tie an old subject to this week, scored 1.37 (n=17). a16z: date hooks appear in 3 of 17 outliers and 0 of 16 weakest posts. Its Roblox 20th-anniversary archive carousel hit 60.46x.
transfers.twist: Build the canon at onboarding from Wikidata and Geektime's own archive: the Israeli tech canon of exits, IPOs, launches and founding dates, each date checked against the filing or the original press release. Each post pairs one little-known documented fact with a present-day stake (what the company or its alumni do now, a current price or headcount). Use the house template, as a single image or a 2-slide hook-then-receipt on the navy and lime plate. Slide 1 is an archival product or founder photo with an actor + verb + consequence card headline of 5 to 9 Hebrew words. Slide 2 is the primary-source receipt: the original announcement, or Geektime's own headline from that year, as a screenshot. The caption runs 300 to 650 characters with at most 1 hashtag and a photo credit.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: It works through recognition plus a fact nobody else posts that day. Readers already know the subject, the lookup is free, and nobody can scoop it. Geektime's audience rewards named-maker stories (its own B6 4.11x; Wired's ZuckOff 17.35x), and Geektime's own archive is a primary source its competitors do not hold.
transfers.risk: Geektime's flat posts are the ones with no local stake or fresh reason (a global Google feature scored 0.57x), so a bare 'X years ago' reads as filler. Nostalgia saturates: the music aggregators' nostalgic share fell from 29% to 24%, and nostalgia ran 0.70 on Don Techno's own page. Archival photos raise rights questions. The Hebrew copy has to stay dry.
transfers.experiment: TRY in the experiment slot: 4 anniversary posts over 4 weeks, one a week, each on the exact date, each with a present-day stake line, all on the house news template. Metric: (likes + 3 x comments) as a multiple of Geektime's own median for posts of the same age, read at 48 to 96 h (comments alone when likes are hidden). Success: a median of at least 1.3x, with at least 2 of 4 above 1.5x. Retire it if 3 of 4 land under 0.7x.

transfers.pattern: Watch one step upstream of the competition and post first, with a saturation penalty when rivals already ran the story
transfers.source_evidence: 17 winning stories were traced back to where they started (14 found). Celebrity stories start on talk shows' own YouTube channels (a Tonight Show clip was up 5 days before edmmusic's 3.25x card). Platform stories start in newsrooms (Spotify removing 75M tracks, via Music Business Worldwide, 10.8x). The first page on a story did 3.25x, and a page 4 hours later did 0.49x. Instagram-born stories reached the big pages 3.5 to 4.9 days late.
transfers.twist: Keep an upstream registry for Israeli tech: company newsrooms and investor-relations pages, TASE (Maya) and SEC filings, the Israel Innovation Authority, Apple and Samsung Israel price pages and importers, and founders' and VCs' X and LinkedIn accounts. Treat it as saturated when Calcalist, CTech, Globes, TheMarker or Israel Business have already run the story; at 3 or more of them in 7 days, run it only with a new angle. Lead with what changes for the Israeli reader (price, availability, date). Use the 'first publication' label only when it is true and the stake is concrete.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Geektime's own record already shows the payoff: an exclusive with a stake (Israel in Apple's first launch wave) hit 8.54x, and its Israeli-price posts hit 26.5x and 16.11x. News audiences reward whoever posts first. Filings and newsrooms are public, so this takes process, not access.
transfers.risk: Pressure for speed works against accuracy on a news brand. 'First' labels without a stake read as noise. Origin-age ranking means nothing until the engine stops reading hidden likes as 3 and stops treating a 12-post window as the baseline. Verification takes staff time.
transfers.experiment: TRY for 3 weeks: log every news post as 'first' (Geektime posted on Instagram before all 4 competing desks) or 'follower', along with the age of the origin. At least 6 first posts are needed. Success: the first posts' median multiple (own median, 48 to 96 h) is at least 1.5x the follower posts' median, with no correction issued. Fewer than 6 firsts means the registry is not upstream enough: add sources and rerun.

transfers.pattern: Original data as a series: one checkable finding per post, from data only this account owns
transfers.source_industry: Tech news media (data journalism: Wired, Visual Capitalist)
transfers.source_evidence: Wired's original 634-woman survey carousel hit 10.17x: flat charts alternating with verbatim quotes, two type sizes. Visual Capitalist's 26 organic one-comparison charts have a median of 1.89x (US car colours 50.54x), against 0.43x for its partner posts. Beli's ranking 'based on over 120 million ratings' drew 1.41M views. Neil Patel's '37 places AI looks for you' hit 71.45x on one checkable number, while his dense report cards of 78 to 90 words are his weakest posts. The Karos archive: all 29 posts retell someone else's fame, and not one has a subject Karos owns.
transfers.twist: Publish Karos's own 183-account benchmark as a series, one within-account finding per carousel, stated as a count a reader can check. Example: 'Photo-led posts were over-represented among the best posts in 99 accounts and among the weakest in 26.' The cover carries the number and the claim in 7 words or fewer. Each interior slide shows one real best-versus-weakest pair from a single account side by side (B2B comparison lift 3.33), credited 'via @', with 15 to 25 words. Use the orange marker once, on the number. The method line goes in DM Mono. Close on the finding, with no follow card. Never name Karos clients or show their unpublished work.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Only Karos can say it. That fixes the archive's missing owned subject and the bio's unproven promise. A checkable number is the mechanic behind the Neil Patel and Visual Capitalist posts, and marketers save reference data about their own craft.
transfers.risk: Overclaiming: these are sign tests with small effects (mean differences of 0.06 to 0.23), and the skeptics killed several conclusions. Every post must state its n and avoid causal words. Showing other accounts' posts needs credit or permission. At 22 followers, the Karos account cannot prove much on its own. Dense report cards are a known loser.
transfers.experiment: TRY 3 study posts over 3 weeks, alternating with 3 standard Karos carousels. Karos owns the account, so read Insights at 7 days: saves + shares per account reached, and reach among non-followers. Success: the study posts' median saves + shares per reach is at least 1.5x the standard carousels', and at least one study post reaches 3x or more the follower count. Cross-post to LinkedIn as a second read, not a substitute.

transfers.pattern: Typographic manifesto: one line per slide at one size on alternating grounds, built as fact-then-consequence pairs that lead to a thesis
transfers.source_evidence: a16z's manifestos went 3 for 4 at 2x (median 4.68x). 'The builder who can pitch.' hit 12.45x with 7 slides, one centred line per slide and one type size. The first-hires fact-then-consequence carousel hit 5.45x. Karos's only point-of-view post (the Kairos launch) was its most-commented. The B2B set rewards the conversational register (7+/1-) and covers without a logo (8+/1-).
transfers.twist: Use the Karos system: Spectral 600, charcoal alternating with paper, one sentence per slide at one size. Each line is a dated, sourced fact followed by its consequence, which follows Albert's rule of no aphorism without a fact. A possible spine for the Kairos thesis: a campaign that shipped at the right moment against one that shipped late, with dates and results. 6 to 10 slides. The orange marker appears once in the whole carousel, on the turn. No eyebrow naming the series, no end card, and the sources go in the caption's last line.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A manifesto pulls because it is a point of view the reader can repeat. Fact pairs make it checkable, which the archive's 12 'X, not Y' antitheses and interchangeable closers were not. It needs no photography, which solves Karos's thin supply of rights-clean images.
transfers.risk: The copy can drift back to the aphorisms the owner has already rejected. a16z's manifestos ride a 210k audience and a famous brand. One-line slides on charcoal can bring back the flat dark grid (64 of 82 slides were flat charcoal in the 28 Jul batch). Every pair needs a verified source.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 manifestos within 4 weeks, read against the owned-data series and the standard carousels in Insights at 7 days. Every slide must pass the copy gate by carrying a year, a name or a number. Success: shares per reach at least 1.5x the standard carousels' median. Kill it if both land below the standard median.

transfers.pattern: Cover shows a real photograph of the object itself, not a designed brand plate
transfers.source_industry: luxury hospitality & residences (supported by Tech news media)
transfers.source_evidence: Within-account lift for photo-dominant posts: luxury +0.50 in 10 of 10 accounts (p=0.002), Hebrew tech news 10+/1- (p=0.01), all 183 accounts 99+/26-. In Brazilian finance, the two biggest multiples (Nath Financas 31.5x and 26.75x) put the object on the cover: a card machine, real price tags. Hurst Capital's on-brand dark-and-gold carousels, which open on abstract questions, reached 0 of 13 outliers.
transfers.twist: Keep XO's navy and cream system for the interior slides. Make each cover a real photograph of what the rule or product touches: the card machine, a printed duplicata or nota fiscal, the WhatsApp screen of the XOdo flow, or a named small-business owner whose receivable was financed (with consent). Put it under a navy scrim with the two-tone Plus Jakarta headline as one complete pt-BR sentence that states the stake, in 12 words or fewer. No stock or generic AI images; the capybara stays the only non-photo.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: The stake becomes visible in under a second, which is what the fintech kit's winning covers do. XO's branded explainers sit in a flat band of 5 to 18 likes, the typical signature of a designed plate.
transfers.risk: CVM advertising rules: no imagery that implies guaranteed returns, and the disclaimer is required. XO has no photo shoot, so supply is thin, and any business owner shown must consent. The navy and cream alternation is XO's real house system and must not be diluted.
transfers.experiment: TRY 4 carousels over 4 weeks as 2 topic-matched pairs, one photo cover and one plate cover in each pair. Metric: (likes + 3 x comments) against XO's own median at 96 h, plus non-follower reach in Insights. Success: the photo cover beats its paired plate cover by at least 1.5x in both pairs. Make it XO's default after 2 more photo covers land above XO's median.

transfers.pattern: Upstream first-mover sourcing applied to rule changes, posted within 24 h as a claim-plus-proof explainer
transfers.source_evidence: Music: the first mover got 3.25x against 0.49x for a page 4 hours later, and 2-slide claim-plus-proof cards beat 3 to 5 slides on 4 of 4 pages. Brazilian finance: rule-change explainers are the category's biggest multiples (Nath Financas 31.5x, 26.75x), and Tokeniza's CVM working-group card reached 2.0x.
transfers.twist: Keep a registry of the Diario Oficial da Uniao, CVM resolutions and the tokenization working group, Banco Central resolutions (Drex, receivables registration), Receita Federal, and the Sebrae/MEI rule pages. Post within 24 h of publication, in one of two forms. The first is a 2-slide claim-plus-proof: the cover states the rule in the second person with its date, over a photo of the object; slide 2 is the official text as a screenshot with the act's number. The second is the full Nath skeleton: O que muda / Mas atencao / O que fazer. It counts as saturated if InfoMoney, Nath Financas or Me Poupe already posted, and then runs only with an angle specific to receivables. The CVM disclaimer goes on the last slide.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A rule change carries a personal stake and a date, so the first clear explainer collects the saves and shares. Music shows that first mover wins, and Brazilian finance shows that this spine is the category's best format.
transfers.risk: Compliance review slows a 24-hour target, and misreading a decree is worse for a regulated brand than being late. XO's niche (receivables and tokenization) has fewer rule changes than consumer finance, perhaps 1 or 2 a month.
transfers.experiment: TRY every qualifying rule change for 6 weeks (3 to 6 are expected), each posted within 24 h. Metric: own-median multiple at 96 h, plus saves in Insights. Success: a median of at least 1.5x and at least one post at 3x or more. If fewer than 3 events arrive, extend the window rather than lower the bar.

transfers.pattern: An owned character as the host of a recurring series that carries product proof
transfers.source_evidence: Sintra.ai gives each agent its own colour-coded 3D character and uses a 5-slide proof template; 'Meet Soshie' hit 8.26x (537 likes, 102 comments). Across the study, the only AI imagery that wins is an owned character (L1-02). XO's capybara reels are its only content that reaches non-followers: 9,902, 5,433 and 2,841 views against 136 to 142 for its branded reels (top post 36.78x on 385 followers).
transfers.twist: Make the capybara a named, recurring host instead of a one-off meme. On slide 1 or the reel's opening, it reacts to a real event, with the POV joke in the caption and no text on the image. Then 2 to 4 navy and cream plates carry one fact each about receivables or a rule change, with the CVM disclaimer last. The character never states a rate, recommends a product or appears next to return figures.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: An owned character is recognisable at thumbnail size and travels to non-followers, which XO's branded posts do not. Sintra shows that a character system can carry product proof, not just jokes.
transfers.risk: Humour next to investing may read as unserious to investors. The mascot's reach may come from meme fans rather than investors, so follower quality needs watching. AI imagery has to be labelled. The hybrid format may lose the reel's reach.
transfers.experiment: TRY 4 posts over 4 weeks: 2 reels and 2 carousels. Metrics: reel views against XO's branded-reel median (about 140), carousels against XO's own median multiple, plus follows and profile visits in Insights. Success: reels reach at least 3x the branded-reel median, carousels reach at least 1.3x the carousel median, and follows per 1k views do not fall below the pure-meme reels'.

transfers.pattern: Archival 'then' carousel: real period material in date order with almost no added type, ending on today
transfers.source_industry: Startup / founder programs (a16z), supported by Music media & nightlife
transfers.source_evidence: a16z's archival carousels about famous companies went 5 for 5 at 2x (median 9.49x), with 0 to 6 written words per slide; Roblox's archive hit 60.46x. In music, the story behind a known record makes up about 40% of outliers (median 3.5x). In apparel, the best posts are occasions rather than product (SKIMS: 6 of 6 best).
transfers.twist: Use Hanky Panky's own archive, dated from the client's records: the founding story behind the name, the first Signature Lace pieces, old catalogue pages and press clippings, in date order. Words appear on slide 1 only: 8 or fewer in Relais Display at about 52 to 60 px, with no logo. The interior slides carry no words. Close on today's Signature Lace in a saturated colour, worn by a real woman. The caption carries the dated history; long captions win in apparel (8+/0-). Post on a real date: the brand anniversary or National Underwear Day (5 Aug).
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Heritage is the one subject young DTC peers such as SKIMS and Savage X Fenty cannot post. Archival material is real imagery in a category that punishes AI and stock, and recognition works in every industry studied.
transfers.risk: The archive may be thin, and old ads raise rights and model-consent questions. Dated body norms clash with the brand's size-inclusive present. Muted archival colour conflicts with the saturated-colour rule (vivid pixels in 64% of best posts against 39% of weakest), so the last slide must bring the colour back. The client has to supply the material.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 archive posts within 6 weeks, each on a real date. Metric: (likes + 3 x comments) against Hanky Panky's own median at 96 h. Success: both posts at 1.3x or more, and one at 2x or more. Kill it if both land under 0.8x.

transfers.pattern: A named staff member on a dated occasion, told as a wordless staff-in-action sequence
transfers.source_evidence: Le Bristol: all 6 outliers centre a named person or character on a real occasion (Veronique, housekeeper for 35 years, in Housekeeping Week; the cat Socrate on International Cat Day; a newly awarded pastry chef), and all 6 weakest are unpeopled product or decor shots. Gstaad Palace's owner and chef reels hit 23x and 11.6x, and its 6-slide staff-in-action carousel has no text on any slide. Kinfolk's tours of named practitioners are its most reliable driver.
transfers.twist: Show the people who make the product: a 4 to 6 slide sequence from the workroom with no words on the slides (cutting the lace, dyeing the colours, the finishing table), led by one named maker and her years with the company. Peg it to a dated occasion, such as the brand anniversary or a staff anniversary. The cover carries 8 words or fewer and no logo. The caption uses Hanky Panky's cheeky one-liner voice plus 2 factual sentences. Run it only if the client confirms where the product is made and by whom.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Luxury shows that shots of inventory lose and named people on an occasion win, even in a product-led category. Hanky Panky's own winners are candid, laughing women rather than product plates, so a candid maker fits the register.
transfers.risk: Any manufacturing claim must be verified, and staff must consent. This audience follows for product and bodies, so a workroom story may trail the wear shots. It needs a shoot.
transfers.experiment: TRY 1 carousel and 1 reel cutdown within 8 weeks. Success: the carousel reaches 1.3x or more of the own median, and the reel reaches 1.5x or more of Hanky Panky's reel median views. Otherwise, keep it as annual heritage content only.

transfers.pattern: Personalisation carousel: 'which X fits your Y', one pairing per slide on a fixed layout
transfers.source_evidence: Mindtrip's 'Where You Should Travel Based on Your Hobby' hit 29.7x: 9 slides, an 8-word personalisation cover, one hobby-to-city pair per slide on an unchanging layout. It is the largest carousel outlier against a clean baseline. In apparel, a question beat a statement on the same template (OEAK: 118 likes against 7), and TomboyX's numbered product grid closed a post at 14x. Comment prompts win 8+/0- in Kindly's benchmark set (p=0.008).
transfers.twist: 'Your day, your bra.' The cover asks, in 8 words or fewer, which Kindly bra fits your day. Each following slide shows one moment (a long-haul flight, a 12-hour shift, the gym, Sunday at home) paired with one Wave 1 style, worn by a real woman, with women across the size range over the series. Each slide carries 6 words or fewer, since the apparel kit keeps interior slides nearly wordless. Close on a numbered grid of the 4 styles with their size ranges. The caption asks which one is your day.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: The reader finds herself in the list, which drives saves and shares. The answer is the product, so it sells without a pitch. Kindly's peers show that an explicit, answerable ask is its strongest lever.
transfers.risk: This is blocked until the portal record carries Kindly's real profile (L3-04: the prep record is a parked gifting domain) and its own fonts.
