With only 4 styles, there are few slides to fill. It needs real bodies: no AI, which matters in a category where Aerie's #NotAI pledge drew 45,841 likes.
transfers.experiment: After the profile fix, TRY 2 posts over 4 weeks. Metric: (likes + 3 x comments) against the own median at 96 h (comments alone where likes are hidden), plus saves. Success: a median of 1.5x or more, and at least one post with 20 or more comments. Retire it after 2 posts below 0.8x.

transfers.pattern: The named person behind the place, published as an Instagram Collab
transfers.source_industry: luxury hospitality & residences (Collab evidence from Music media and Startup programs)
transfers.source_evidence: Le Bristol: 6 of 6 outliers are a named person or character, and 6 of 6 weakest are unpeopled. Cheval Blanc's two-property crossover posts doubled the tagged audience. Collab lift: music pages 1.37 against 0.98 for solo posts; programme accounts 1.38x against 0.85x, with 40% against 15% of posts reaching 2x.
transfers.twist: Put each creator-map spot's owner or bartender in frame, with their name and years on the corner: 8 or fewer on-photo words in Gaegu, plus the neighbourhood tag. Inset the spot's app place card as proof. Publish as an Instagram Collab with the venue and the mapping creator, so the post lands on three grids. The creator stays the hero, and the owner is the detail.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Sitti's winners are a named person plus a place. Luxury shows that named people beat empty inventory, and Collab is the largest free reach lever in the study, at a time when Sitti has 615 followers.
transfers.risk: Venues must consent and schedule, and some will decline a Collab. An owner portrait can slide into ad register. It adds production load for a small team.
transfers.experiment: TRY 3 Collab carousels over 3 weeks, compared with Sitti's last 3 non-Collab carousels. Metrics: (likes + 3 x comments) against the own median at 96 h, and views against follower count. Success: a median of 1.5x or more, and at least one post reaching 5x the follower count or more.

transfers.pattern: A ranking built from owned data, with a credibility line, as the whole graphic
transfers.source_industry: Tech news media (Visual Capitalist data graphics)
transfers.source_evidence: Visual Capitalist's organic single-comparison charts have a median of 1.89x against 0.43x for its partner posts. In Sitti's own category, the Infatuation's photo-free quadrant chart hit 8.2x with 470 comments, and Beli's ranked list 'based on over 120 million ratings' drew 1.41M views and 423 comments.
transfers.twist: 'The most-saved spots in the East Village this month, from Sitti maps.' One ranked list or map is the whole graphic, in the style of the app's place cards, with a credibility line giving the real count. The caption asks one specific question ('Which one is missing?'). Rank by the number of creators who mapped a spot until Sitti's save counts are large enough to be honest.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: In this category, an opinionated graphic with real names beats photo posts and turns a list into an argument in the comments. Owned data is something competitors cannot copy.
transfers.risk: Thin data makes the claim embarrassing (for example, 'based on 14 saves'). The category's reference accounts hide likes, so their multiples are weak evidence. Venues left off the list may be annoyed.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 posts within 6 weeks. Success: comments at 3x or more of Sitti's median comments, and a multiple of 1.5x or more. Retire it if both land below 1x.

transfers.pattern: An all-video carousel of one night from several angles, with a label only after slide 1
transfers.source_evidence: On the music pages, all-video carousels have a median of 1.52 (n=45), and those with 6 to 7 video slides reach 2.02 (n=10). Image-then-video 2-slide cards score 1.32 (n=65). In the startup set, Speedrun's text-free kickoff-week diary hit 8.2x. The Pitch hides its likes, so plays are its usable metric: the solo reel median is 354, against 9.9k to 17.8k for the posts co-published with @getdeel.
transfers.target: The Pitch by Deel (Startup / founder programs)
transfers.twist: Tell one regional final as a 6 to 7 slide all-video carousel from the programme's own footage: the room filling, a founder mid-pitch, a judge's question, the announcement, the check. Use MP4 slides with the original audio. Slide 1 carries the only headline, 5 words or fewer naming the city and the winner, in the v4 kit (Inter, Stage ground, one lilac word). Every other slide gets only a small label such as 'SINGAPORE · 12 MAY'. Publish as a Collab with the winner. The 2027 waitlist goes in the caption's last line, and prize wording stays exact.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Real event footage is the category's strongest material, and The Pitch owns seven finals of it. Moving slides drive completion and replays. Collabs are what drive The Pitch's plays.
transfers.risk: It needs footage the programme owns and founder consent. The engine renders PNG plates only, so video slides need a build path. The finals are in the past, so the peg has to be an anniversary or the 2027 season. A Collab lift can be mistaken for a format lift.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 all-video carousels over 4 weeks, from two different cities, each as a Collab. Metric: plays against The Pitch's solo reel median (354), plus carousel reach in Insights. Success: both reach 5x or more (1.8k plays or more). Record the lift as a Collab effect unless a non-Collab repeat also clears 3x.

transfers.pattern: A named person plus one real number on the cover, with the primary artifact as proof
transfers.source_evidence: Stan's post on an ER nurse's $45 Japan guide ('$85,235 in two weeks') hit 23.0x with 746 comments, and its sequel hit 17.0x. The cover leads with the number, and slide 6 shows the real storefront card as proof. In the startup set, join_ef's named founders hit 119x, and Startup World Cup's photo of the winners holding the check hit 150x as a Collab.
transfers.target: The Pitch by Deel (Startup / founder programs)
transfers.twist: Tell a verified winner's path. The cover names the founder and one verified number from after the stage (a round raised, customers, hires) over their photo. The slides follow the application, a still from the two-minute pitch, the result, and the proof artifact (the founder's own announcement post or a press screenshot). Prize wording stays exactly 'up to $50,000 SAFE'. Publish as a Collab with the founder. There is no comment ask, since comment prompts do not lift in the startup set.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A real person and a real number make the outcome feel reachable to applicants. The founder's own artifact is proof The Pitch does not have to claim for itself.
transfers.risk: It can imply that The Pitch caused the raise, which needs brand and legal sign-off. It must never name or imply a global champion. Only verified, nameable winners can be used.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 posts over 6 weeks. Metrics: carousel reach and shares in Insights, and plays for any reel cutdown. Success: reach at 3x or more of The Pitch's recent carousel median, on both posts.

transfers.pattern: A rule-change explainer with the catch before the reassurance and a concrete action
transfers.source_evidence: Nath Financas's decree carousels hit 31.5x and 26.75x. The cover states the rule and its date over the object, and the slides follow O que muda / Mas atencao (the vetoed penalty) / what to do. In music, the only two posts with over 6,000 comments were a study and a platform policy, and Spotify removing 75M tracks hit 10.8x.
transfers.twist: When a scene rule changes (Ibiza or Berlin licensing and noise rules, festival bag and ticket policies, Spotify, Beatport or SoundCloud payout rules, a city's club closing hours), post a 2-slide card in Don Techno's STORY preset. Slide 1: an eyebrow with source and date, the kicker, and the rule as one spoken sentence over real footage of the place. Slide 2: what changes for you, and the catch (the exception or the vetoed clause). The source goes in the caption, the credit line is mandatory, and there is no call to action.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A rule with a date gives ravers and DJs a personal stake. The scene's most-commented posts already come from policies and studies, yet music media rarely packages policy as an explainer.
transfers.risk: Don Techno's audience is a party audience (Latin and deep house), so policy may read as dry. The sources must pass verify_sources.py. Rules in Madrid or Ibiza may not interest the global audience.
transfers.experiment: TRY in Don Techno's weekly exploration slot: 3 rule-change posts over 6 weeks. Metric: the comment index (likes are hidden on 82 of Don Techno's 102 posts from 2026) against its own quarterly median, at 96 h or more. Success: a median of 1.3 or more and one post at 2.0 or more. Retire it after 3 posts below 0.7, per the formats.yaml contract.

transfers.pattern: A finite, answerable question, followed by a post that shows the real tally
transfers.source_evidence: Comment prompts win in 11 of 12 apparel accounts (+0.32, p=0.006). Knix's question of the day, which closed on a whiteboard photo of the team's hand tally, drew 107 comments (3.8x its median). In music, comment prompts appear in only 3.7% of posts and have never been tested. A 'has X sold out?' question drew 564 comments. Don Techno hides its likes, so comments carry its measurement.
transfers.twist: Ask a finite scene question with a real answer set, never an open 'thoughts?'. For example: which closing track at a named festival this summer, with 4 named candidates as label slides over footage. The question goes in the caption's first line, with no emoji and no exclamation mark. A week later, a follow-up post shows the real count (a screenshot of the comment totals) with the winning clip.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A question with named options is cheap to answer, and a tally post proves someone read the replies. Both feed the comment signal Don Techno already depends on.
transfers.risk: It conflicts with the owner's rule that Don Techno captions carry no call to action, so it needs his sign-off. The market's taste is not Don Techno's audience's taste. Anything that reads as engagement farming risks reach under Meta's ranking rules.
transfers.experiment: TRY only in the exploration slot, and only with the owner's sign-off: 2 question posts and their tally follow-ups over 4 weeks. Success: a comment index of 2x or more of Don Techno's own median on both questions, and the follow-up at 1.0 or more. Otherwise drop it.

transfers.pattern: First with the official date: an upstream registry and first-mover posting of season facts
transfers.source_industry: Music media & nightlife (supported by luxury hospitality: @courchevel_officiel)
transfers.source_evidence: In music, the first page on a story did 3.25x and a page 4 hours later did 0.49x. Among Courchevel's official account's outliers are pre-season anticipation posts ('Dans 3 mois', a J-100 countdown) timed to the ski audience. Luxury posts led by the photograph win 10 of 10.
transfers.twist: Keep a registry of official Courchevel sources: Courchevel Tourisme, the lift operator's opening calendar, the ESF ski school, race calendars, Meteo-France snow bulletins, the altiport. Publish the date on the day it is announced, as one complete, verified French sentence, with the source in the footer band, over a winter photo with snow. Use the V3 system (pierre, encre, bordeaux, ardoise; Instrument Serif headings, no italic). No prices and no competitor hotels. A follow-up post runs only when there is a new fact, never as a countdown for its own sake.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A ski audience plans around dates. Being first with a checkable date is the one timely lane a new account with few photos can win, and it satisfies Albert's rule of a fact the reader can use.
transfers.risk: Dates move with the snow and operator decisions, and a wrong date damages a luxury brand. N°3 has no engagement measurement yet (no scraper token). Stand-in photos must be licensed and show snow. The official account remains the source of record, so N°3 must add its own framing.
transfers.experiment: TRY across the 2026-27 pre-season (October to December): every official date announcement posted within 24 h (4 to 8 are expected). Prerequisite: switch on a weekly public-grid read of @n3courchevel. Success: the season posts' median multiple is 1.5x or more of N°3's other lanes, and saves + shares in the Insights the client exports are 2x or more. If measurement is still off in November, run it as a draft-only lane and judge on the client's feedback.

transfers.pattern: Archival 'then' carousel for a place, pegged to an anniversary
transfers.source_industry: Startup / founder programs (a16z), supported by Music media & nightlife
transfers.source_evidence: a16z's archival carousels went 5 for 5 at 2x (median 9.49x); the Roblox archive hit 60.46x with no added type. In music, the story behind a known record makes up about 40% of outliers (median 3.5x). In luxury, Sotheby's outliers include a named-provenance hook ('once home to Henry Ford II').
transfers.twist: The histoire lane, adapted to Albert's copy rule. Public-domain or licensed archive photos of Courchevel 1850 (the resort's founding years, the first lifts, the altiport, the early ski schools, with dates verified from the Savoie archives), one per slide in date order, full-bleed. Each slide carries one complete French sentence in the footer band saying who, what and when, with no italic and no roman numerals. The cover names the subject and the year. Post on the event's anniversary and close on the same place today, in snow. Competitor hotels are never the subject.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: Archive material gives real imagery to an account with no photo shoot. The place's own legend is the luxury equivalent of the founder archive, and dated facts fit the address-book rule.
transfers.risk: Albert judged the Saulire sample 'not hot enough', so history must be pegged to a date or to current news. Archive rights are uncertain. Sepia images clash with the V3 palette. The audience mostly wants the current season.
transfers.experiment: TRY 2 pegged histoire posts during the season. Success: 1.3x or more of N°3's own median once measurement is live. Otherwise, keep histoire as a minority lane (at most 1 post in 5).

transfers.pattern: A visible choice game built from the brand's own material
transfers.source_evidence: Aerie's 'which one is aerie green?' drew 10.69x with 1,326 comments and no product photo, and Commando's version hit 2.84x. Luxury accounts ask for comments in only 3.6% of posts, and within luxury the lift is +0.167 over just 3 accounts. Courchevel's official tag-a-friend giveaway drew 984 comments.
transfers.twist: A sober knowledge game built from real photographs, with no prize and no emoji. For example: four summits seen from Courchevel 1850, and the question 'which one is Mont Blanc?' in one complete sentence. The answer, with one fact about the summit, comes in the next carnet post. Use the V3 system with no numbered badges; letters in the caption only.
transfers.why_it_should_transfer: A game that is visible in the image and costs nothing to play creates conversation in a category that almost never asks for it, and it keeps the address book's promise of useful facts.
transfers.risk: Games can cheapen an ultra-luxury register. N°3 has no measurement yet. With few followers, a low comment count could look empty.
transfers.experiment: TRY 1 post in the season, and only once measurement is live. Success: comments at 5x or more of N°3's median comments, with no drop in follows. Otherwise, do not repeat it.

advancement.strongest_at: Design craft and restraint. Highest mean craft in the study (7.38 on the enrichment batch's 10-point scale; archdigest 9, kinfolk 8.5, gstaadpalace/oetkerhotels/chevalblanc 8). Almost no decorative furniture: 6 device uses across 96 best posts. It also has the strongest sign-consistent result in the study: photo-dominant colour +0.50 within-account, 10+/0-, p=0.002. Best posts use one text size (7+/1-) and often no sentence at all (5+/1-); carousels lead (49 of 96). Caveat: mean_craft comes from two tagging batches on different scales (the original six industries top out at 4, the enrichment/n3/music accounts at 9), so craft only ranks within a batch. This ranking also uses device load, layout entropy and how many sign-consistent winners each industry has.
advancement.weakest_at: Format innovation. It has the lowest best-post layout entropy (1.76 bits): one look repeated, and 'other' covers 49 of 96 best posts. Hooks are thin: 4 accounts with no hook scored -0.67, hype loses (1+/6-), and single images lose (1+/7-).

advancement.strongest_at: Editorial voice and the formats built on it. Craft 6.33/10 (don.techno, defected, mixmag, 6am all 7). Authoritative/expert register 7+/0- (p=0.016), hype 0+/7- (p=0.016), long captions 6+/0- (p=0.031), bright designed colour 0+/6-. Carousels lead (33 of 54 best), with almost no devices. Don Techno's own audit adds two measured formats: the 2-slide claim+proof and the all-video carousel (1.52x). Story-behind-a-record on the anniversary accounts for 40% of outliers.
advancement.weakest_at: Reels (0+/3-) and layout variety (entropy 2.3 bits). The whole system depends on footage the page doesn't own, and hidden likes on 22-77% of posts weaken the counts. Don Techno's redesign is still unproven (first weekly analysis due 27 Sep).

advancement.strongest_at: Hooks and news-design discipline. Top craft in the original batch (3.38; wired 5, themarker, morningbrew, visualcap 4). Five sign-consistent winners, the most of any original-batch industry: photo-dominant 10+/1- (p=0.012), medium-contrast plates 0+/8- (p=0.008), muted 0+/8-, dark 1+/9- (p=0.02), high contrast 6+/0- (p=0.031). News with a reader stake 8+/2-, big number 3+/0-, and best covers run 3 words longer than weak ones (median; 9+/2-). The client's own product-in-hand price posts reach 26.5x.
advancement.weakest_at: Video and format innovation. Reels lose (2+/8-) and single images dominate. Partner logos (2+/7-) and how-to hooks (0+/4-) lose, and house-programme promos sit at the bottom of every publisher's feed.

advancement.strongest_at: Hook and community mechanics on real-body photography. The clearest CTA result in the study: comment prompt 11+/1- (p=0.006). Also story hook 10+/1- (p=0.012), mixed sentence form 12+/2- (p=0.013), long captions 8+/0- (p=0.008), no hook 0+/7-, short captions 1+/12- (p=0.003). Six sign-consistent winners, the most of any industry, led by SKIMS, Savage X Fenty and Aerie. Finite-choice quiz cards (118 vs 7 likes on the same template) and product-cut-out grids are its format inventions.
advancement.weakest_at: On-image typography and designed cards. Product-shot covers don't separate best from weakest (5+/7-), spec-sheet infographics lose, and our posts ran 9 type sizes. Median ER is the lowest in the set (0.026%, big-follower brands). The long-caption and comment signals are inflated by giveaway and contest posts.

advancement.strongest_at: Restraint and recognition. No devices 8+/0- (p=0.008) and condensed display type 0+/9- (p=0.004). Best posts use real place photos (5+/2-), centred or no logo (5+/0-) and quote cards (12 best covers). a16z shows famous founders and archive stories driving 13 of its 17 outliers, including a 60.5x archive post with no added type. Highest median ER in the set (0.288%).
advancement.weakest_at: Too much depends on star power, and generic reels in caption boxes are a16z's weakest posts. News/announcement hooks lean negative (3+/6-). Hidden likes on @deelpitch leave no usable client baseline.

advancement.strongest_at: Format innovation. The widest spread of best-post layouts in the study (3.11 bits), plus side-by-side comparisons (4+/1-; reputeforge's colours-vs-shades carousel at 19.18x), named repeatable series, huge headlines (7+/1-), one text size (6+/1-), brand-colour accent (5+/1-) and no logo (8+/1-, p=0.039).
advancement.weakest_at: Design restraint. Its best posts carry the heaviest decorative load in the study (boxes/cards 19, pills 19, icons 7 across 78 posts), and these devices lose on all accounts (boxes 24+/54-, icons 18+/38-). Muted palettes lose (1+/8-, p=0.039). Median craft is only average (3.29), and small accounts dominate (@karoslabs has 22 followers).

advancement.strongest_at: Narrative hooks with a named person and a real number (story 6+/1-, emotional register 5+/0-, comment prompt 7+/1-, huge headline 4+/1-). Stan's named-creator Nina story reached 23x.
advancement.weakest_at: Design range. Layout entropy is low (2.05 bits; 39 of 71 best covers are full-bleed photo + headline) and no signal reaches p<0.05. Pills (1+/6-), icons (0+/3-), dark mood (0+/5-), hype (1+/5-) and link-in-bio (1+/5-) all lose, and platform-theory posts score 0.15-0.23x.

advancement.industry: Fintech / investing (xodigital; Brazil peers and fintech leaders)
advancement.strongest_at: Data-built graphics and type. Condensed/display sans 7+/1- (Brazil peers). Other-brand and regulator logos used as borrowed authority 6+/1-. Long reference captions 8+/3-. Save/share on reference content 3+/1-. The leaders (nubank, btgpactual, c6bank, exame) add emotional register 7+/2- and no devices 11+/2- (p=0.022).
advancement.weakest_at: Design craft. It has the lowest craft in both batches (Brazil peers 3.08 on the 4-point scale, leaders 5.88 on the 10-point scale), and the Brazil peers' best posts carry the most decorative furniture in the study (22 boxes, 12 icons, 9 pills across 72). Boxes lose among the leaders (0+/8-, p=0.008), as do stock photos (0+/6-, p=0.031) and plain sans (2+/10-, p=0.039). Hooks default to hype and listicle counts.

advancement.strongest_at: Design. The photography and the order of the photos are the whole craft. Photo-dominant posts win in 10 of 10 accounts (+0.50, sign p=0.002), the strongest industry signal in the study. Carousels are photo essays with no text that move from a wide establishing shot to a detail to the setting (Oetker villa, 3 slides, 13.87x; Relais & Chateaux, 9 to 10 slide essays; Cheval Blanc, 11 angles on one fireworks night, 24.97x). There are no graphic devices. Named staff and characters appear on dated occasions: all 6 of Le Bristol's outliers are a named person or its cat Socrate on a real occasion, and Gstaad Palace's owner and chef reels hit 23x and 11.6x. The ranking is a qualitative judgement: the craft scores from the two labelling batches use different scales and are not compared.
advancement.weakest_at: Ideation and conversation. Only 3.6% of posts ask for a comment. The weakest slots are filled with shots of empty rooms. Event and advocacy posts break the register, and franchises wear out (AD's New American Voices fell from 0.41x to 0.14x). News gets buried under decorative type.

advancement.strongest_at: Ideation and trend sourcing. About 40% of outliers are the story behind a well-known record, looked up and posted on its anniversary (median 3.5x). Stories are traced upstream: the first page to run one hit 3.25x, and a page 4 hours later got 0.49x. Instagram-born stories reached the big pages 3.5 to 4.9 days late. Repeat windows are measured rather than guessed. A 2-slide claim-plus-proof card beat 3 to 5 slides on all 4 pages that post both. The authoritative register (7+/0-) and long captions (6+/0-) win.
advancement.weakest_at: Design range and conversation. The pages use no graphics on purpose and take their colour from the footage; saturated designed colour loses (0+/6-). Comment prompts are almost absent (3.7% of posts, never tested). The aggregator habit of reposting other people's clips does not carry over to brands. Several findings flipped between periods, including best reel length and best weekday.

advancement.strongest_at: Editorial marketing built on recognition. a16z's archival 'then' carousels went 5 for 5 at 2x (median 9.49x). Its one-line typographic manifestos went 3 for 4 (median 4.68x). Slides with no graphic devices win 8+/0- (p=0.008). Collab posts do 1.38x against 0.85x for solo posts. Covers deliver the payoff in about 5 words, and 13 of a16z's 17 outliers centre a famous founder or company.
advancement.weakest_at: Self-promotion and teaching. Posts about the programme itself make up 10 of a16z's 16 weakest. Talking-head and banner reels have a median of 0.19x, and term explainers went 0 for 5. Condensed display type loses 0+/9-. Comment prompts do not help here.

advancement.strongest_at: Getting people to take part. Comment prompts win in 11 of 12 accounts (+0.32, p=0.006). A swatch quiz reached 10.69x (Aerie) and 2.84x (Commando). Asking a question instead of making a statement drew 118 likes against 7 on the same template. A question-of-the-day that closes on a hand tally drew 107 comments (Knix). Graphics are built from the product itself (TomboyX's numbered grid 14x, cut-out boards 2.91x). Interior slides carry no words, and posts hook onto dated moments.
advancement.weakest_at: Authority and storytelling depth. Product-on-model shots with seasonal copy fill the weakest slots (all 6 of SKIMS's weakest). Short captions lose (1+/12-). Dense pitch boards score 0.52x. Heritage and maker stories are rarely told.

advancement.strongest_at: Keeping a regulated category human. The emotional or personal register wins (+0.28, 7+/2-). Slides with no graphic devices win (11+/2-, p=0.02). Boxes and cards lose (0+/8-, p=0.008), and stock photos lose in every account that uses them (0+/6-). Real photography of people leads.
advancement.weakest_at: Type defaults and conversation. The default sans-serif loses (2+/10-) and medium text contrast loses (3+/11-). Only 8% of posts ask for a comment.

advancement.strongest_at: Packaging news. Photo-dominant posts win 10+/1- (p=0.01), and high-contrast headline cards win (medium contrast loses 0+/8-). Morning Brew's carousels of primary-source screenshots scored 3.36x to 3.79x. Visual Capitalist's one-glance comparison charts have an organic median of 1.89x against 0.43x for its partner posts. Exclusivity labels work when a real stake backs them (Geektime's scoop, 8.54x).
advancement.weakest_at: Reels (2+/8-), how-to posts (0+/4-), illustration (1+/6-), and partner or in-house promotion. Sourcing is reactive: there is no anniversary engine and no one-step-upstream registry.

advancement.strongest_at: The product as the graphic, and personalisation. Mindtrip's hobby-to-city carousel hit 29.7x. App place cards and save counts serve as social proof. The Infatuation's quadrant chart hit 8.2x with 470 comments, and Beli's data-backed ranking drew 1.41M views. A named creator plus a real number works (Stan, 23x, 746 comments). Comment prompts win 7+/1-.
advancement.weakest_at: Layout range. Its best-layout entropy of 2.05 bits is the lowest of the original sets, and 39 of 71 best covers are the same full-bleed photo with a headline. 'Monetise your recommendations' pitches score 0.15x to 0.23x. Dark palettes lose (0+/5-) and hype loses (1+/5-).

advancement.strongest_at: Rule-change explainers with a personal stake. Nath Financas's decree carousels hit 31.5x and 26.75x. Monthly proof-of-payment reports work, and disclosing the late payments first reached 3.42x (Inco). Condensed display type wins 7+/1-. Me Poupe's 15-slide decades carousel shows metronomic pacing at 28.35x.
advancement.weakest_at: Branded plates and abstract-question carousels (Hurst Capital: 0 of 13 reached outlier status), stock photos, decorative pills. The emotional or personal register is barely used (7.6% of posts, no lift). Authority is borrowed only in text, never shown as the object itself.

advancement.strongest_at: Comparison modules built from real brand assets (Reputeforge, 19.18x and 8.83x), fixed case-card modules (The Brand Blueprint, 11.03x), and showing what the AI product produced (Sintra, 8.26x). Covers without a logo win 8+/1- (p=0.04), and the conversational register wins 7+/1-.
advancement.weakest_at: Owned subjects and emotion. All 29 posts in Karos's archive retell someone else's fame, with riddle covers and the template's skeleton showing through. Only 6.4% of posts use an emotional or personal register. Muted palettes lose 1+/8-. The live Karos account has 22 followers and cannot validate anything yet.

notes: Code defect (the faces that paint), not a performance claim, so there is nothing to test statistically. Code-only is the right layer, and the provenance (7 of 7 runs, the Google-only link emitter, the recorded-versus-painted gap) is specific.
A face the kit declares (including a licensed or flagged substitute listed in the kit) counts as the client's face. Only an engine or browser fallback that the kit does not declare fails the render.
Legal and script-coverage constraint. No statistic applies, and the L1 MUST is the right extent because licences and glyph coverage are the same for every client.
A substitute the kit states wins over genre matching. Genre matching applies only when the kit names none.
Owner standard. L1 is correct because the defect it prevents (an engine blind to the client's language) showed up in all 7 clients, across unrelated industries.
Owner standard at the right layer. No client is harmed; it is the precondition that stops L1 defaults from overriding the kits.
Code defect with three independent instances in three industries (GoDaddy parking page, Cloudflare 403, Yotpo widget). Code-only is correct.
This is a code defect and it is correctly scoped. It removes harm (Kindly gifting content, fonts read from Cloudflare and Yotpo pages).
Per-client data fixes. L3 is the right layer and no breadth question arises.
Correct L3 data fix. Kindly's L3 rules already gate the agent on the record.
Ship as an owner standard (L1 MUST) and drop the performance citation, or cite only that 4+ sizes never wins. Do not describe the size count as a measured lever for carousels.

The ban covers oversized numerals that are not the message (the 220px class). Small index or step numerals that the client kit defines are allowed, and they count as the meta or label tier, not a third size.
Legibility floor, and the evidence correctly shows that headline size itself is null. A constraint needs no breadth test.
The legibility floor holds and the cover-headline kit override is present. For Hebrew, which has no caps, the 26-28px meta exception never applies, so Hebrew meta stays at 30px or more. That is fine.
Owner typesetting standard with no performance claim attached. L1 MUST is fine.
Mandated legal or status text, source lines and compliance lines never move to the caption. The overflow ladder takes body sentences only.

Owner standard, so not refutable. The bans are well supported: in the 89-account data, fragments lose even among accounts where reels are not over-represented in the best set (12+/28-, p=0.017), and hype loses there too (11+/25-, p=0.029). The breadth caveats are already noted: complete sentences are 0+/6- in luxury (p=0.031) and hype is null in intimates (6+/6-) and leans positive in startup (4+/2-). The rule is authored, not measured, for those industries.

Exempt the client's registered or trademarked claims and mandated legal labels. Apply the 'Not' opener ban to English (and to 'Não X. É Y.' frames), not to ordinary negation in other locales. The product, pack or colour shown in the image counts as the fact.
Code defect (figures role unset). Code-only is correct.
Engine and fallback faces never set numerals. A client-kit mono may set indices, source dates and regulation codes where the kit assigns it. Story numbers use the figures or display role.
Owner standard plus blame by provenance: the gradients came from the bundled L1 templates. The layer is correct.
Correct, and it protects clients. Kit-supplied gradient artwork (The Pitch v4's gradient bands and panels) is the client's own and stays allowed.

Keep 'a device must carry a fact or show the product' as an authored standard through D-1, DS-08 and owner point M. Treat 'the default slide has no device' as a TRY at L1, excluded for intimate apparel, until a carousel-only within-account test passes.

The rule applies to devices the engine chooses. A container in the client's captured design language (its house card, tab, badge or backer) is not 'decorative' for this rule. Neither is a legally required status badge.

Owner standard, and the performance data are null, as stated. The 'cover and closer only' DEFAULT is, if anything, supported by the client-industry subset: logo top-left is -0.12 over 45 accounts (12+/27-, p=0.024) in the 89-account data, and B2B logo-none is 8+/1-. Note that fintech & investing leans the other way (top-left 10+/3-, logo-none 4+/8-), so a fintech kit could override the corner and frequency.

The kit's stated position, size and lockup win, including tabs and badges the kit defines. Top-start plus equal-area is the default only when the kit is silent. For RTL, the logo sits below the counter band. 'Never on a plate' covers engine-invented plates, not the kit's own tab or badge.
Code defect plus an owner rule. Code-only is correct.
Code defect. The layer is right, and it enforces the owner's logo rule.
Owner standard (onboarding decides logo treatment), with failures in three separate clients. L1 is fine.

Onboarding may derive candidate variants only. Once staff approve them they become kit files, and render never recolours or strips a logo. Where the client supplies light and dark variants (Kindly, The Pitch), no derivation runs.

Holds at breadth and survives the format check. Medium contrast is 6+/27- (p<0.001) among the 89-account data's accounts where reels are not over-represented, and it is negative in 7 of 9 industries. Intimates (4+/2-) and creator (2+/3-) are near-null, but as a legibility constraint it applies everywhere anyway.

MUST: measured 4.5:1 (3:1 at 72px and up) against the worst 10% of pixels. The shade's polarity opposes the text colour. An opaque kit plate or backer counts as a shade. A translucent light wash under light text is banned.

Owner standard, correctly labelled as not a performance lever. Tech news reverses (best covers carry +3 words, 9+/2-), so the Geektime kit may need a higher cap within the 20-word total. That is a parameter, not a refutation.
The 8-word title cap is an L1 default that a kit may raise slightly (Geektime Hebrew to 9) within the 20-word total.

The most robust performance result in the set. It holds in the 89-account data both where reels dominate the best set (14+/5-) and where they do not (30+/11-, p=0.004), so it is not a reel artefact. Muted/neutral also holds where reels do not dominate (9+/30-). Only luxury (p=0.002) and Hebrew news (p=0.012) are individually significant, and Brazil fintech (5+/4-) and startup (4+/3-) are flat, but the pooled result and the leave-one-industry-out result support L1 DEFAULT. The famous-subject confound remains.
Holds at L1 as a DEFAULT, with no client harmed. N3 grades stand-in photos to its palette at the client's request, so 'photo-dominant' must not be read as 'never grade'.
Code defect (render key, orphaned slides). Code-only is correct.
Code defect, correctly scoped.
Authored standard at DEFAULT, and it correctly declines the refuted 'variety' claim. There are no breadth issues.
A DEFAULT that fits the pinned-system kits. It conflicts with nothing, because The Pitch's alternation rule and XO's spine live inside the pinned system.
Measurement defect with evidence across four industries (music, startup, intimates, creator). Code-only is correct, and it is a precondition for every performance row.
Code defect. The layer is right, and it has to land before any published or outlier-driven claim.

Process standard. One caveat: 6-9 peers per client is underpowered for industry-level claims (the design's own power figure is about 14 accounts for a 70% chance to detect x1.5), so peer studies should feed L2 pools rather than make standalone per-client verdicts.
The default holds. TOP-02 already stops peer patterns from steering a client without confirmation from the client's own grid.
Rests on primary platform statements, not on our benchmark. Slide count is correctly left null. DEFAULT is fine.
Primary-research default. No harm.

Story/named-subject hook at L1 DEFAULT. How-to demotion only for low-involvement consumer accounts and publishers, not for the B2B, fintech, startup or luxury kits. Promo demotion stays DEFAULT with the date/price/free/named-person exception.
The price hook is available only where the kit permits prices in posts (not N3).
Remove link-in-bio closers at L1. Follow/save end-card removal is an authored or owner default, not a measured one.
A kit-stated closer (a publisher's article pointer, a regulated CTA with a risk line) overrides the default. Comment asks exclude 'comment X to enter' mechanics.
Brand-integrity and platform constraint, correctly not tied to the null AI-image statistic. L1 MUST is fine.
Brand-integrity constraint. It is consistent with every kit (XO's capybara, Geektime's labelled AI concept art, The Pitch's and Sitti's no-AI rules).
Owner standard, correctly labelled as thin in data (9 accounts). The budgets are kit parameters, and the layer is fine.
Mandated compliance text is excluded from the word budget and the hard cap.

Owner mechanism at DEFAULT, with the icon half correctly capped by the data. Chart covers are neutral (11+/12-) and B2B big-number covers are 0+/4-, so code-built graphics should not default to a numeral cover in B2B.
A DEFAULT. It matches Karos's fact graphic per slide and XO's icon pills. No harm.
Client data fix. L3 is correct.
L3 data fix. Correct, and it blocks X-13 and any Pitch work until it lands.
Drop condensed display as a candidate for startup/founder programs (The Pitch) and luxury (N°3). It may go only to fintech-like targets. Mark story and emotional register for B2B as low prior.
Each candidate must pass the target client's L3 hard lines and kit (fonts, palette, logo, caption caps, compliance) before it takes an experiment slot.
Code defect (the what-works loop has no producer). Code-only is correct.
Code defect. Correct.
Credit line on every post: DEFAULT. Collab only when a reachable partner is featured, at TRY at L1.
A credit line is required when third-party media is used. A collaborator is named only where a consenting public partner exists.
Architecture standard. No breadth question arises.
Architecture standard. It is what protects clients: L3 beats L2 beats L1, with hard lines winning.
